3.3.s:
..śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ.....
śrīgurubhyo namaḥ .. ..
atha brahmottarakhaṃḍamāraṃbhaḥ ..
.. oṃ namaḥ śivāya .. ..
jyotirmātrasvarūpāya nirmalajñānacakṣuṣe ..
namaḥ śivāya śāṃtāya brahmaṇe liṃgamūrttaye .. 1 ..
3.3.d:
..श्रीगणेशाय नमः.....
श्रीगुरुभ्यो नमः .. ..
अथ ब्रह्मोत्तरखंडमारंभः ..
.. ओं नमः शिवाय .. ..
ज्योतिर्मात्रस्वरूपाय निर्मलज्ञानचक्षुषे ..
नमः शिवाय शांताय ब्रह्मणे लिंगमूर्त्तये .. 1 ..
3.3.m: Salutation to venerable Gaṇeśa. / Salutation to the venerable Gurus. / Now begins the Brahmottarakhaṇḍa. / Oṃ, salutation to Śiva. / To the one whose nature is pure light, who has the eye of spotless knowledge, / salutation to Śiva, peaceful, the absolute, embodied as the liṅga. (1)

3.3.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
ākhyātaṃ bhavatā sūta viṣṇormāhātmyamuttamam..
samastāghaharaṃ puṇyaṃ samasena śrutaṃ ca naḥ.. 2..
3.3.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
आख्यातं भवता सूत विष्णोर्माहात्म्यमुत्तमम्..
समस्ताघहरं पुण्यं समसेन श्रुतं च नः.. 2..
3.3.m: The seers said: / You have recounted, O Sūta, the supreme māhātmya of Viṣṇu, / which removes all sins and brings merit, and it has been heard by us in brief. (2)

3.3.s:
idānīṃ śrotumicchāmo māhātmyaṃ tripuradviṣaḥ ..
tadbhaktānāṃ ca māhātmyamaśeṣāghaharaṃ param.. 3..
3.3.d:
इदानीं श्रोतुमिच्छामो माहात्म्यं त्रिपुरद्विषः ..
तद्भक्तानां च माहात्म्यमशेषाघहरं परम्.. 3..
3.3.m: Now we wish to hear the māhātmya of the enemy of Tripura, / and the supreme māhātmya of his devotees, which removes all sins, 3

3.3.s:
tanmaṃtrāṇāṃ ca māhātmyaṃ tathaiva dvijasattama ..
tatkathāyāśca tadbhakteḥ prabhāvamanuvarṇaya.. 4..
3.3.d:
तन्मंत्राणां च माहात्म्यं तथैव द्विजसत्तम ..
तत्कथायाश्च तद्भक्तेः प्रभावमनुवर्णय.. 4..
3.3.m: and likewise the māhātmya of his mantras, O best of the twice-born. / Relate also the majesty of stories about him and devotion to him. 4

3.3.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
etāvadeva martyānāṃ paraṃ śreyaḥ sanātanam..
yadīśvarakathāyāṃ vai jātā bhaktirahaitukī .. 5..
3.3.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एतावदेव मर्त्यानां परं श्रेयः सनातनम्..
यदीश्वरकथायां वै जाता भक्तिरहैतुकी .. 5..
3.3.m: Sūta said: / This alone is the mortals' supreme and eternal welfare, / namely, that unmotivated devotion should arise towards tales of Īśvara. 5

3.3.s:
atastadbhaktileśasya māhātmyaṃ varṇyate mayā ..
api kalpāyuṣā nālaṃ vaktuṃ vistarataḥ kvacit.. 6..
3.3.d:
अतस्तद्भक्तिलेशस्य माहात्म्यं वर्ण्यते मया ..
अपि कल्पायुषा नालं वक्तुं विस्तरतः क्वचित्.. 6..
3.3.m: Therefore, even a fraction of the māhātmya of devotion to him is described by me; / for even in a lifespan of a kalpa it could nowhere be told at length. 6

3.3.s:
sarveṣāmapi puṇyānāṃ sarveṣāṃ śreyasāmapi ..
sarveṣāmapi yajñānāṃ japayajñaḥ paraḥ smṛtaḥ.. 7..
3.3.d:
सर्वेषामपि पुण्यानां सर्वेषां श्रेयसामपि ..
सर्वेषामपि यज्ञानां जपयज्ञः परः स्मृतः.. 7..
3.3.m: Among all merits, among all goods, / and among all sacrifices, the sacrifice of mantra repetition is regarded as supreme. 7

3.3.s:
tatrādau japayajñasya phalaṃ svastyayanaṃ mahat ..
śaivaṃ ṣaḍakṣaraṃ divyaṃ maṃtramāhurmaharṣayaḥ.. 8..
3.3.d:
तत्रादौ जपयज्ञस्य फलं स्वस्त्ययनं महत् ..
शैवं षडक्षरं दिव्यं मंत्रमाहुर्महर्षयः.. 8..
3.3.m: There, first of all, the fruit of the sacrifice of mantra repetition is a great blessing of welfare; / the great seers call the six-syllabled Śaiva [utterance] the divine mantra. 8

3.3.s:
devānāṃ paramo devo yathā vai tripurāṃtakaḥ ..
maṃtrāṇāṃ paramo maṃtrastathā śaivaḥ ṣaḍakṣaraḥ .. 9..
3.3.d:
देवानां परमो देवो यथा वै त्रिपुरांतकः ..
मंत्राणां परमो मंत्रस्तथा शैवः षडक्षरः .. 9..
3.3.m: Just as the destroyer of Tripura is indeed the supreme god among the gods, / so the Śaiva six-syllabled [mantra] is the supreme mantra among mantras. 9

3.3.s:
eṣa paṃcākṣaro maṃtro japtṝṇāṃ muktidāyakaḥ..
saṃsevyate muniśreṣṭhairaśeṣaiḥ siddhikāṃkṣibhiḥ..3.3.1.10
10 .. asyaivākṣaramāhātmyaṃ nālaṃ vaktuṃ caturmukhaḥ..
3.3.d:
एष पंचाक्षरो मंत्रो जप्तॄणां मुक्तिदायकः..
संसेव्यते मुनिश्रेष्ठैरशेषैः सिद्धिकांक्षिभिः..3.3.1.10
10 .. अस्यैवाक्षरमाहात्म्यं नालं वक्तुं चतुर्मुखः..
3.3.m: This five-syllabled mantra grants liberation to those who chant it; / it is constantly served by the best of sages, by all who desire accomplishments. / Even the four-faced [Brahmā] is not capable of reciting the greatness of its syllables. 10
wherein the scriptures have reached their final conclusion, supremely blissful. 11

3.3.s:
sarvajñaḥ paripūrṇaśca saccidānaṃdalakṣaṇaḥ ..
sa śivo yatra ramate śaive paṃcākṣare śubhe .. 12 ..
3.3.d:
सर्वज्ञः परिपूर्णश्च सच्चिदानंदलक्षणः ..
स शिवो यत्र रमते शैवे पंचाक्षरे शुभे .. 12 ..
3.3.m: Omniscient, complete, characterized by existence, consciousness, and bliss— / that Śiva delights in the auspicious five-syllabled Śaiva [mantra]. 12

3.3.s:
etena maṃtrarājena sarvopaniṣadātmanā ..
lebhire munayaḥ sarve paraṃ brahma nirāmayam..13..
3.3.d:
एतेन मंत्रराजेन सर्वोपनिषदात्मना ..
लेभिरे मुनयः सर्वे परं ब्रह्म निरामयम्..13..
3.3.m: By means of this king of mantras, the essence of all the Upaniṣads, / all the sages attained the supreme, disease-free Brahman. 13

3.3.s:
namaskāreṇa jīvatvaṃ śive'tra paramātmani ..
aikyaṃ gatamato maṃtraḥ parabrahmamayo hyasau .. 14 ..
3.3.d:
नमस्कारेण जीवत्वं शिवेऽत्र परमात्मनि ..
ऐक्यं गतमतो मंत्रः परब्रह्ममयो ह्यसौ .. 14 ..
3.3.m: Through the bow of greeting, the state of the individual soul merges into unity with Śiva here, the Supreme Self; / therefore, this mantra indeed consists of the supreme Brahman. 14

3.3.s:
bhavapāśanibaddhānāṃ dehināṃ hitakāmyayā ..
āhoṃnamaḥ śivāyeti maṃtramādyaṃ śivaḥ svayam .. 15..
3.3.d:
भवपाशनिबद्धानां देहिनां हितकाम्यया ..
आहोंनमः शिवायेति मंत्रमाद्यं शिवः स्वयम् .. 15..
3.3.m: Desiring the welfare of embodied beings bound by the fetters of mundane existence, / Śiva himself uttered the primeval mantra: 'Oṃ namaḥ śivāya'. 15

3.3.s:
kiṃ tasya bahubhirmaṃtraiḥ kiṃ tīrthaiḥ kiṃ tapo'dhvaraiḥ ..
yasyoṃnamaḥ śivāyeti maṃtro hṛdayagocaraḥ.. 16 ..
3.3.d:
किं तस्य बहुभिर्मंत्रैः किं तीर्थैः किं तपोऽध्वरैः ..
यस्योंनमः शिवायेति मंत्रो हृदयगोचरः.. 16 ..
3.3.m: What need has he of many mantras, what of sacred fords, what of austerities and sacrifices, / in whose heart the mantra 'Oṃ namaḥ śivāya' dwells? 16

3.3.s:
tāvadbhramaṃti saṃsāre dāruṇe duḥkhasaṃkule ..
yāvannoccārayaṃtīmaṃ maṃtraṃ dehabhṛtaḥ sakṛt .. 17 ..
3.3.d:
तावद्भ्रमंति संसारे दारुणे दुःखसंकुले ..
यावन्नोच्चारयंतीमं मंत्रं देहभृतः सकृत् .. 17 ..
3.3.m: Embodied beings wander in mundane existence, dreadful and filled with sorrow, / only so long as they do not utter this mantra even once. 17

3.3.s:
maṃtrādhirājarājo'yaṃ sarvavedāṃtaśekharaḥ ..
sarvajñānanidhānaṃ ca so'yaṃ caiva ṣaḍakṣaraḥ .. 18 ..
3.3.d:
मंत्राधिराजराजोऽयं सर्ववेदांतशेखरः ..
सर्वज्ञाननिधानं च सोऽयं चैव षडक्षरः .. 18 ..
3.3.m: This is the king over sovereign mantras, the crest of all the Vedāntas, / and this six-syllabled one is the repository of all knowledge. 18
This six-syllabled mantra is the lamp on the path to liberation, the submarine fire to the ocean of ignorance, / [and] the forest fire to heinous sins! 19

3.3.s:
tasmātsarvaprado maṃtraḥ so'yaṃ pañcākṣaraḥ smṛtaḥ ..
strībhiḥ śūdraiśca saṃkīrṇairdhāryate muktikāṃkṣibhiḥ..3.3.120 ..
nāsya dīkṣā na homaśca na saṃskāro na tarpaṇam ..
na kālo nopadeśaśca sadā śucirayaṃ manuḥ .. 21 ..
mahāpātakavicchittyai śiva ityakṣaradvayam ..
alaṃ namaskiyāyukto muktaye parikalpate .. 22..
upadiṣṭaḥ sadguruṇā japtaḥ kṣetre ca pāvane ..
sadyo yathepsitāṃ siddhiṃ dadātīti kimadbhutam .. 23 ..
ataḥ sadgurumāśritya grāhyo'yaṃ maṃtranāyakaḥ..
puṇyakṣetreṣu japtavyaḥ sadyaḥ siddhiṃ prayacchati .. 24..
guravo nirmalāḥ śāṃtāḥ sādhavo mitabhāṣiṇaḥ ..
kāmakrodhavinirmuktāḥ sadācārā jiteṃdriyāḥ .. 25 ..
etaiḥ kāruṇyato datto maṃtraḥ kṣipraṃ prasiddhyati ..
kṣetrāṇi japayogyāni samāsātkathayāmyaham .. 26 ..
3.3.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रदो मंत्रः सोऽयं पञ्चाक्षरः स्मृतः ..
स्त्रीभिः शूद्रैश्च संकीर्णैर्धार्यते मुक्तिकांक्षिभिः..3.3.120 ..
नास्य दीक्षा न होमश्च न संस्कारो न तर्पणम् ..
न कालो नोपदेशश्च सदा शुचिरयं मनुः .. 21 ..
महापातकविच्छित्त्यै शिव इत्यक्षरद्वयम् ..
अलं नमस्कियायुक्तो मुक्तये परिकल्पते .. 22..
उपदिष्टः सद्गुरुणा जप्तः क्षेत्रे च पावने ..
सद्यो यथेप्सितां सिद्धिं ददातीति किमद्भुतम् .. 23 ..
अतः सद्गुरुमाश्रित्य ग्राह्योऽयं मंत्रनायकः..
पुण्यक्षेत्रेषु जप्तव्यः सद्यः सिद्धिं प्रयच्छति .. 24..
गुरवो निर्मलाः शांताः साधवो मितभाषिणः ..
कामक्रोधविनिर्मुक्ताः सदाचारा जितेंद्रियाः .. 25 ..
एतैः कारुण्यतो दत्तो मंत्रः क्षिप्रं प्रसिद्ध्यति ..
क्षेत्राणि जपयोग्यानि समासात्कथयाम्यहम् .. 26 ..
3.3.m:
Therefore, this five-syllabled mantra is held to grant everything; / it may be maintained by women, śūdras, and people of mixed castes who desire liberation. 20
It requires no initiation, no oblation into fire, no preparatory rite, no water offering, / no specific time, and no formal instruction; this mantra is always pure. 21
For the destruction of heinous sins, the two syllables 'Śi-va' / are sufficient; coupled with homage, it is fit for liberation. 22
When taught by a true guru and chanted in a purifying sacred field, / it immediately grants the desired accomplishment—what wonder is there in this? 23
Therefore, having resorted to a true guru, this sovereign of mantras should be received; / it should be chanted in holy sacred fields: it grants immediate accomplishment. 24
Gurus are pure, tranquil, virtuous, of measured speech, / free from desire and anger, of righteous conduct, having their senses conquered. 25
When bestowed out of compassion by these [teachers], the mantra quickly yields success. / I shall tell concisely of the sacred fields suitable for mantra repetition. 26

3.3.s:
prayāgaṃ puṣkaraṃ ramyaṃ kedāraṃ setubaṃdhanam ..
gokarṇaṃ naimiṣāraṇyaṃ sadyaḥ siddhikaraṃ nṛṇām ..27..
atrānuvarṇyate sadbhiritihāsaḥ purātanaḥ..
asakṛdvā sakṛdvāpi śṛṇvatāṃ maṃgalapradaḥ.. 28..
mathurāyāṃ yaduśreṣṭho dāśārha iti viśrutaḥ ..
babhūva rājā matimānmahotsāho mahābalaḥ .. 29 ..
śāstrajño nayavākchūro dhairyavānamitadyutiḥ ..
apradhṛṣyaḥ sugaṃbhīraḥ saṃgrāmeṣvanivarttitaḥ .. 3.3.1.30..
mahāratho maheṣvāso nānāśāstrārthakovidaḥ..
vadānyo rūpasaṃpanno yuvā lakṣa ṇasaṃyutaḥ .. 31 ..
sa kāśirājatanayāmupayeme varānanām ..
kāṃtāṃ kalāvatīṃ nāma rūpaśīlaguṇānvitām .. 32 ..
kṛtodvāhaḥ sa rājeṃdraḥ saṃprāpya nijamaṃdiram..
rātrau tāṃ śayanārūḍhāṃ saṃgamāya samāhvayat .. 33 ..
sā svabhartrā samāhūtā bahuśaḥ prārthitā satī ..
na babaṃdha manastasminna cāgaccha tadaṃtikam.. 34..
3.3.d:
प्रयागं पुष्करं रम्यं केदारं सेतुबंधनम् ..
गोकर्णं नैमिषारण्यं सद्यः सिद्धिकरं नृणाम् ..27..
अत्रानुवर्ण्यते सद्भिरितिहासः पुरातनः..
असकृद्वा सकृद्वापि शृण्वतां मंगलप्रदः.. 28..
मथुरायां यदुश्रेष्ठो दाशार्ह इति विश्रुतः ..
बभूव राजा मतिमान्महोत्साहो महाबलः .. 29 ..
शास्त्रज्ञो नयवाक्छूरो धैर्यवानमितद्युतिः ..
अप्रधृष्यः सुगंभीरः संग्रामेष्वनिवर्त्तितः .. 3.3.1.30..
महारथो महेष्वासो नानाशास्त्रार्थकोविदः..
वदान्यो रूपसंपन्नो युवा लक्ष णसंयुतः .. 31 ..
स काशिराजतनयामुपयेमे वराननाम् ..
कांतां कलावतीं नाम रूपशीलगुणान्विताम् .. 32 ..
कृतोद्वाहः स राजेंद्रः संप्राप्य निजमंदिरम्..
रात्रौ तां शयनारूढां संगमाय समाह्वयत् .. 33 ..
सा स्वभर्त्रा समाहूता बहुशः प्रार्थिता सती ..
न बबंध मनस्तस्मिन्न चागच्छ तदंतिकम्.. 34..
3.3.m:
Prayāga, delightful Puṣkara, Kedāra, Setubandha, / Gokarṇa, and Naimiṣāraṇya immediately bring accomplishment to men. 27
Here an ancient legend is recounted by the virtuous, / which brings blessings to those who hear it, whether repeatedly or even once. 28
In Mathurā, there was an eminent Yadu known as Dāśārha, / a king wise, of great energy, and possessing great strength. 29
He knew the scriptures, spoke with prudence, was heroic, resolute, of immeasurable splendor, / unconquerable, very deep, never retreating in battles, 30
a great chariot-warrior, a great archer, skilled in the meaning of various treatises, / generous, endowed with beauty, youthful, and marked with auspicious signs. 31
He married the daughter of the king of Kāśī, beautiful of face, / a beloved lady named Kalāvatī, endowed with beauty, good character, and virtues. 32
Having concluded the wedding, that lord of kings reached his own palace; / at night, when she had mounted the bed, he called her for union. 33
Called by her husband and entreated many times, the virtuous woman / did not fix her mind on him, nor did she approach his side. 34

3.3.s:
saṃgamāya yadāhūtā nāgatā nijavallabhā ..
balādāhartukāmastāmudatiṣṭhanmahīpatiḥ .. 35 ...
.. rājñyuvāca .. ..
mā māṃ spṛśa mahārāja kāraṇajñāṃ vrate sthitām ..
dharmādharmau vijānāsi mā kārṣīḥ sāhasaṃ mayi .. 36 ..
kvacitpriyeṇa bhuktaṃ yadrocate tu manīṣiṇām ..
daṃpatyoḥ prītiyogena saṃgamaḥ prītivarddhanaḥ .. 37 ..
priyaṃ yadā me jāyeta tadā saṃgastu te mayi ..
kā prītiḥ kiṃ sukhaṃ puṃsāṃ balādbhogena yoṣitām .. 38 ..
aprītāṃ rogiṇīṃ nārīmaṃtarvatnīṃ dhṛtavratām ..
rajasvalāmakāmāṃ ca na kāmeta balātpumān .. 39 ..
prīṇanaṃ lālanaṃ poṣaṃ raṃjanaṃ mārdavaṃ dayām..
kṛtvā vadhūmupagamedyuvatīṃ premavānpatiḥ ..
yuvatau kusume caiva vidheyaṃ sukhamicchatā .. 3.3.1.40 .
ityukto'pi tayā sādhvyā sa rājā smaravihvalaḥ ..
balādākṛṣya tāṃ haste parirebhe riraṃsayā .. 41 ..
3.3.d:
संगमाय यदाहूता नागता निजवल्लभा ..
बलादाहर्तुकामस्तामुदतिष्ठन्महीपतिः .. 35 ...
.. राज्ञ्युवाच .. ..
मा मां स्पृश महाराज कारणज्ञां व्रते स्थिताम् ..
धर्माधर्मौ विजानासि मा कार्षीः साहसं मयि .. 36 ..
क्वचित्प्रियेण भुक्तं यद्रोचते तु मनीषिणाम् ..
दंपत्योः प्रीतियोगेन संगमः प्रीतिवर्द्धनः .. 37 ..
प्रियं यदा मे जायेत तदा संगस्तु ते मयि ..
का प्रीतिः किं सुखं पुंसां बलाद्भोगेन योषिताम् .. 38 ..
अप्रीतां रोगिणीं नारीमंतर्वत्नीं धृतव्रताम् ..
रजस्वलामकामां च न कामेत बलात्पुमान् .. 39 ..
प्रीणनं लालनं पोषं रंजनं मार्दवं दयाम्..
कृत्वा वधूमुपगमेद्युवतीं प्रेमवान्पतिः ..

3.3.m:
When his beloved wife did not come though called for union, / the king stood up, desiring to seize her by force. 35
The queen said: / Do not touch me, O great king, [me] who know the cause and stand observing a vow; / you know righteousness and unrighteousness—do not commit rash violence against me. 36
What is enjoyed by the beloved sometimes pleases the wise; / union through the love of both husband and wife increases love. 37
When love arises in me, then your union may take place with me; / what love, what pleasure is there for men in enjoying women by force? 38
A man should not forcefully lust after a woman who is unwilling, diseased, pregnant, / observing a vow, menstruating, or without desire. 39
Having shown pleasing, fondling, nurturing, delighting, gentleness, and pity, / an affectionate husband should approach his bride, a young woman; / one who desires pleasure should act [gently] toward a young woman as toward a flower. / Though addressed in this way by that virtuous woman, the king, overcome with passion, / dragged her by the hand with force and embraced her, desiring to make love. 40–41

प्रत्युवाच विहस्यैनं विनयेन शुचिस्मिता .. 44 ..

3.3.m:
As soon as she was touched, she was like a heated lump of iron; / feeling as though he were burning, he let go, distraught with fear. 42
The king said: / Ah, a very great wonder has been seen in you, my dear! / How has your body, tender as a leaf-bud, become like fire? 43
The king was thus greatly astonished and afraid; the king's beloved, / smiling purely, laughed and replied to him with modesty. 44
The queen said: / O king, formerly in my childhood, Durvāsas, the foremost of sages, / out of compassion imparted to me the five-syllabled Śaiva teaching. 45
By the power of that mantra my body is freed from defilement; / it cannot be touched by sinful men abandoned by fate.
By your nature, O king, unchaste women, courtesans, and the like— / women constantly addicted to tasting liquor—are always enjoyed by you.
Ritual ablution is not performed daily, the pure mantra is not recited, / [and] Īśāna is not worshipped by you; how are you fit to touch me?

3.3.m:
The king said: / Tell me that auspicious five-syllabled Śaiva lore, O fair-hipped one; / having sins destroyed by that lore, I desire pleasure with you, my beloved.
The queen said: / I must not initiate you, for you are my master. / Approach the guru Garga, O king, the best among knowers of mantras.
Sūta said: / Thus conversing, the husband and wife approached the presence of Garga, / and bowed down to his feet with their heads, their hands joined in reverence.
Then the king, having repeatedly worshipped the pleased guru, / with a humble mind declared the secret desire of his heart:
The king said: / Make me fulfilled, O guru, as I have approached you, your mind tender with compassion; / you ought to teach [me] the five-syllabled Śaiva lore.
Give me that mantra, O guru, by which that sin may be cleansed, / whatever has been done unknowingly or knowingly through royal acts.
Thus requested by the king, Garga, the best among brahmins, / led the two of them to the most excellent, highly sacred bank of the Kālindī.

3.3.s:

तन्मस्तके करं न्यस्य ददौ मंत्रं शिवात्मकम् .. .. 57..
तन्मंत्रधारणादेव तद्गुरोर्हस्तसंगमात्..
निर्ययुस्तस्य वपुषो वायसाः शतकोटयः .. 58..

भस्मीभूतास्ततः सर्वे दृश्यंते स्म सहस्रशः .. 59..

राजा च राजमहिषी तं गुरुं पर्यपृच्छताम् .. 3.3.1.60 ..
भगवन्निदमाश्चर्यं कथं जातं शरीरतः ..
वायसानां कुलं दृष्टं किमेतत्साधु भण्यताम् .. 61 ..

3.3.m:
There, seated himself at the base of a sacred tree, the guru, / to the king who had bathed in the water of the sacred ford and had fasted,
having seated him facing east and bowed to Śiva's lotus feet, / placed his hand on his head and imparted the mantra consisting of Śiva.
Merely from holding that mantra, and from the touch of that guru's hand, / hundreds of millions of crows came forth from his body.
With scorched wings, screeching, falling to the surface of the earth, / they were all then seen in thousands, reduced to ashes.
Seeing that flock of crows burning, both exceedingly amazed, / the king and the royal queen questioned that guru:
O venerable one, how did this wonder arise from the body? / A flock of crows was seen; explain truly what this is!
The venerable guru said: O king, as you wandered through thousands of births, / endless sins were accumulated in manifold ways.

तथा पापीयसीं योनिं क्वचित्पापेन गच्छति ..
साम्ये पुण्यान्ययोश्चैव मानुषीं योनिमाप्तवान् .. 64 ..
शैवी पंचाक्षरी विद्या यदा ते हृदयं गता.
अघानां कोटयस्त्वत्तः काकरूपेण निर्गताः .. 69..
कोटयो ब्रह्महत्यानामगम्यागम्यकोटयः..
स्वर्णस्तेयसुरापानभ्रूणहत्या दिकोटयः ..
भवकोटिसहस्रेषु येऽन्ये पातकराशयः .. 66..

आसंस्तवाद्य राजेंद्र दग्धाः पातककोटयः .. .. 67 ..
अनया सह पूतात्मा विहरस्व यथासुखम् ..

गुरुवर्यमनुज्ञाप्य मुदितौ तौ च दंपती .. 69..
3.3.m:
Whatever merits you had across those thousands of births, / by their preponderance one is born somewhere in virtuous wombs.
Likewise, one goes to a most sinful womb somewhere on account of sin; / and when merits and demerits are equal, you obtained a human womb.
When the five-syllabled Śaiva lore entered your heart, / millions of sins went forth from you in the form of crows.
Millions of slaughters of brahmins, millions of approaches to women who must not be approached, / millions of thefts of gold, liquor-drinkings, and abortions, / and whatever other heaps of sins across thousands of millions of births—
they are reduced to ashes in an instant when the five-syllabled Śaiva [mantra] is held. / Today, O lord of kings, your millions of sins have been burned away.
With your soul purified, enjoy pleasures with her at your will. / Having spoken thus and taught the mantra, the best of sages,
accompanied by the two whose hearts were amazed, went to his own home; / and having taken leave of the excellent guru, the husband and wife were joyful.

3.3.m:
Then, having reached their palace, the two of great splendour shone. / Firmly embracing his wife, who was cool like sandalwood, / the king attained supreme contentment, like an impoverished man who has gained wealth.
This crown of all the Vedas, Upaniṣads, Purāṇas, and treatises, destroying sin— / the supreme, great power of the five syllables alone has been related in brief by me.
Thus ends the first chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of the Five-syllabled Mantra', in the Brahmottarakhaṇḍa, the third [khaṇḍa] in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

3.3.m: There is nothing superior to this for the purification of sins, / bringing delight to all, glorious, accomplishing all aims and desires,

It is the cause of destruction even of sins that cannot be broken at all times / by the supreme expiations prescribed by great sages.

3.3.d:
इयमेव परं श्रेयः सर्वशास्त्रविनिश्चितम्..
यद्भक्त्या परमेशस्य पूजनं परमो दयम्.. 6..
3.3.m: This alone is the supreme good ascertained by all treatises: / the worship of the Supreme Lord with devotion, which yields supreme prosperity.

3.3.s:
jānatā'jānatā vāpi yena kenāpi hetunā ..
yatkiṃcipi devāya kṛtaṃ karma vimuktidam .. 7 ..
3.3.d:
जानताऽजानता वापि येन केनापि हेतुना ..
यत्किंचिपि देवाय कृतं कर्म विमुक्तिदम् .. 7 ..
3.3.m: Whether knowingly or unknowingly, or for whatever reason, / whatever slight act is performed for God yields complete liberation.

3.3.s:
māghe kṛṣṇacaturddaśyāmupavāso'ti durlabhaḥ..
tatrāpi durlabhaṃ manye rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ nṛṇām .. 8..
3.3.d:
माघे कृष्णचतुर्द्दश्यामुपवासोऽति दुर्लभः..
तत्रापि दुर्लभं मन्ये रात्रौ जागरणं नृणाम् .. 8..
3.3.m: In the month of Māgha, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, fasting is exceedingly rare; / even more difficult than that, I think, is the keeping of a night vigil by men.

3.3.s:
atīva durlabhaṃ manye śivaliṃgasya darśanam ..
sudurlabhataraṃ manye pūjanaṃ parameśituḥ .. .. 9..
3.3.d:
अतीव दुर्लभं मन्ये शिवलिंगस्य दर्शनम् ..
सुदुर्लभतरं मन्ये पूजनं परमेशितुः .. .. 9..
3.3.m: Exceedingly rare, I consider, is the darśana of the Śivaliṅga; / even far rarer, I consider, is the worship of the Supreme Lord.

3.3.s:
bhavakoṭiśatotpannaṣuṇyarāśivipākataḥ..
labhyate vā punastatra bilvapatrārcanaṃ vibhoḥ .. 3.3.2.10 ..
3.3.d:
भवकोटिशतोत्पन्नषुण्यराशिविपाकतः..
लभ्यते वा पुनस्तत्र बिल्वपत्रार्चनं विभोः .. 3.3.2.10 ..
3.3.m: From the ripening of a mass of merit produced across hundreds of millions of births / is obtained, moreover, the worship of the Lord with bilva leaves on that occasion.

3.3.s:
varṣāṇāmayutaṃ yena snātaṃ gaṃgāsarijjale .
sakṛdbilvārcanenaiva tatphalaṃ labhate naraḥ..11..
3.3.d:
वर्षाणामयुतं येन स्नातं गंगासरिज्जले .
सकृद्बिल्वार्चनेनैव तत्फलं लभते नरः..11..
3.3.m: A man who has bathed in the water of the river Gaṅgā for ten thousand years / obtains that [same] fruit merely by worshipping once with a bilva leaf.

3.3.s:
yāniyāni tu puṇyāni līnānīha yugeyuge ..
māghe'sitacaturdaśyāṃ tāni tiṣṭhaṃti kṛtsnaśaḥ .. 12 ..
3.3.d:
यानियानि तु पुण्यानि लीनानीह युगेयुगे ..
माघेऽसितचतुर्दश्यां तानि तिष्ठंति कृत्स्नशः .. 12 ..
3.3.m: Whatever merits have vanished here age after age / all abide entirely on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight in Māgha.

3.3.s:
etāmeva praśaṃsaṃti loke brahmādayaḥ surāḥ ..
munayaśca vaśiṣṭhādyā māghe'sitacaturdaśīm .. 13 ..
3.3.d:
एतामेव प्रशंसंति लोके ब्रह्मादयः सुराः ..
मुनयश्च वशिष्ठाद्या माघेऽसितचतुर्दशीम् .. 13 ..
3.3.m: The gods headed by Brahmā, and sages such as Vasiṣṭha, / praise this very fourteenth of the dark fortnight in Māgha in the world.

3.3.s:
atropavāsaḥ kenāpi kṛtaḥ kratuśatādhikaiḥ ..
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ puṇyaṃ kalpakoṭitapo'dhikam .. 14..
3.3.d:
अत्रोपवासः केनापि कृतः क्रतुशताधिकैः ..
रात्रौ जागरणं पुण्यं कल्पकोटितपोऽधिकम् .. 14..
3.3.m: A fast kept here by anyone surpasses a hundred sacrifices; / the merit of a night vigil is greater than austerity for ten million kalpas.

3.3.s:
ekena bilvapatreṇa śivaliṃgārcanaṃ kṛtam ..
trailokye tasya puṇyasya ko vā sādṛśyamicchati .. 15 ..
3.3.d:
एकेन बिल्वपत्रेण शिवलिंगार्चनं कृतम् ..
त्रैलोक्ये तस्य पुण्यस्य को वा सादृश्यमिच्छति .. 15 ..
3.3.m: If the worship of the Śivaliṅga is performed with a single bilva leaf, / who indeed could seek an equal to that merit in the three worlds?

3.3.s:
atrānuvarṇyate gāthā puṇyā paramaśobhanā ..
gopanīyāpi kāruṇyādgautamena prakāśitā .. 16 ..
3.3.d:
अत्रानुवर्ण्यते गाथा पुण्या परमशोभना ..
गोपनीयापि कारुण्याद्गौतमेन प्रकाशिता .. 16 ..
3.3.m: Here is narrated a sacred, exceedingly splendid tale, / which, though secret, was disclosed by Gautama out of compassion. / 16

3.3.s:
ikṣvākuvaṃśajaḥ śrīmānrājā parama dhārmikaḥ..
āsīnmitrasahonāma śreṣṭhaḥ sarvadhanurbhṛtām.. 17..
3.3.d:
इक्ष्वाकुवंशजः श्रीमान्राजा परम धार्मिकः..
आसीन्मित्रसहोनाम श्रेष्ठः सर्वधनुर्भृताम्.. 17..
3.3.m: Born of the Ikṣvāku lineage was a glorious and supremely righteous king / named Mitrasaha, foremost among all archers. / 17

3.3.s:
sa rājā sakalāstrajñaḥ śāstrajñaḥ śrutipāragaḥ ..
vīro'tyaṃtabalotsāho nityodyogī dayānidhiḥ.. 18..
3.3.d:
स राजा सकलास्त्रज्ञः शास्त्रज्ञः श्रुतिपारगः ..
वीरोऽत्यंतबलोत्साहो नित्योद्योगी दयानिधिः.. 18..
3.3.m: That king knew all weapons, was versed in the scriptures, and had mastered the Vedas; / a hero possessed of immense strength and vigor, ever energetic, a treasury of compassion. / 18

3.3.s:
puṇyānāmiva saṃghātastejasāmiva paṃjaraḥ ..
āścaryāṇāmiva kṣetraṃ yasya mūrtirvirājate .. 19 ..
3.3.d:
पुण्यानामिव संघातस्तेजसामिव पंजरः ..
आश्चर्याणामिव क्षेत्रं यस्य मूर्तिर्विराजते .. 19 ..
3.3.m: As if a mass of merits, as if a cage of fiery splendors, / as if a sacred field of wonders—such did his form shine forth. / 19

3.3.s:
hṛdayaṃ dayayākrāṃtaṃ śriyākrāṃtaṃ ca tadvapuḥ ..
caraṇau yasya sāmaṃtacūḍāmaṇimarīcibhiḥ .. 3.3.2.20 ..
ekadā mṛgayākelilolupaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ ..
viveśa gahvaraṃ ghoraṃ balena mahatāvṛtaḥ .. .. 21 ..
tatra vivyādha viśikhaiḥ śārdūlāngavayānmṛgān ..
rurūnvarāhānmahiṣānmṛgeṃdrānapi bhūriśaḥ .. 22 ..
sa rathī mṛgayāsakto gahanaṃ daṃśita ścaran ..
kamapi jvalanākāraṃ nijaghāna niśācaram .. 23 ..
tasyānujaḥ śucāviṣṭo dṛṣṭvā dūre tirohitaḥ ..
bhrātaraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā ciṃtayāmāsa cetasā .. 24 ..
nanveṣa rājā durddharṣo devānāṃ rakṣasāmapi ..
chadmanaiva prajetavyo mama śatrurna cānyathā .. 25 ..
iti vyavasitaḥ pāpo rākṣaso manujākṛtiḥ ..
āsasāda nṛpaśreṣṭhamutpāta iva mūrtimān .. 26 ..
taṃ vinamrākṛtiṃ dṛṣṭvā bhṛtyatāṃ kartumāgatam ..
cakre mahānasādhyakṣamajñānātsa mahīpatiḥ .. 27 ..
atha tasminvane rājā kiṃcitkālaṃ vihṛtya saḥ ..
nivṛtto mṛgayāṃ hitvā svapurīṃ punarāyayau .. 28 ..
tasya rājeṃdramukhyasya madayaṃtītināmataḥ ..
damayantī nalasyeva viditā vallabhā satī .. 29 ..
etasminsamaye rājā nimaṃtrya munipuṃgavam ..
vaśiṣṭhaṃ gṛhamāninye saṃprāpte pitṛvāsare .. 3.3.2.30 ..
rakṣasā sūdarūpeṇa saṃmiśritanarāmiṣam ..
śākāmiṣaṃ puraḥ kṣiptaṃ dṛṣṭvā gururathābravīt .. 31 ..
dhigdhiṅnarāmiṣaṃ rājaṃ stvayaitacchadmakāriṇā ..
khalenopahṛtaṃ me'dya ato rakṣo bhaviṣyasi .. 32 ..
rakṣaḥkṛtamavijñāya śaptvaivaṃ sa gurustataḥ ..
punarvimṛśya taṃ śāpaṃ cakāra dvādaśābdikam .. 33 ..
rājāpi kopitaḥ prāha yadidaṃ me na ceṣṭitam ..
na jñātaṃ ca vṛthā śapto guruṃ caiva śapāmyaham .. 34 ..
ityapoṃjalinādāya guruṃ śaptuṃ samudyataḥ ..
patitvā pādayostasya madayantī nyavārayat ..35..
tato nivṛttaḥ śāpācca tasyā vacanagauravāt ..
tatyāja pādayoraṃbhaḥ pādau kalmaṣatāṃ gatau ..36..
kalmaṣāṃghririti khyātastataḥ prabhṛti pārthivaḥ ..
babhūva guruśāpena rākṣaso vanagocaraḥ ..37..
sa bibhradrākṣasaṃ rūpaṃ ghoraṃ kālāṃ takopamam ..
cakhāda vividhāñjaṃtūnmānuṣādīnvanecaraḥ ..38..
sa kadācidvane kvāpi ramamāṇau kiśorakau ..
apaśyadaṃtakākāro navoḍhau munidaṃpatī .. ..39..
rākṣaso mānuṣāhāraḥ kiśoramuninaṃdanam ..
jagdhuṃ jagrāha śāpārto vyāghro mṛgaśiśuṃ yathā ..3.3.2.40..
rakṣogṛhītaṃ bhartāraṃ dṛṣṭvā bhītātha tatpriyā ..
uvāca karuṇaṃ bālā kraṃdaṃtī bhṛśavepitā .. 41 ..
bhobho māmā kṛthāḥ pāpaṃ sūryavaṃśayaśodhara ..
madayaṃtīpatistvaṃ hi rājeṃdro na tu rākṣasaḥ ..42..
na khāda mama bharttāraṃ prāṇātpriyatamaṃ prabho ..
ārttānāṃ śaraṇārttānāṃ tvameva hi yato gatiḥ .. 43 ..
pāpānāmiva saṃghātaiḥ kiṃ me duṣṭairjaḍāsubhiḥ ..
dehena cātibhāreṇa vinā bhartrā mahātmanā .. 44 ..
malīmasena pāpena pāṃcabhautena kiṃ sukham ..
bāloyaṃ vedavicchāṃtastapasvī bahuśāstravit .. 45 ..
ato'sya prāṇadānena jagadrakṣā tvayā kṛtā.
kṛpāṃ kuru mahārāja bālāyāṃ brāhmaṇastriyām .. 46 ..
3.3.d:
हृदयं दययाक्रांतं श्रियाक्रांतं च तद्वपुः ..
चरणौ यस्य सामंतचूडामणिमरीचिभिः .. 3.3.2.20 ..
एकदा मृगयाकेलिलोलुपः स महीपतिः ..
विवेश गह्वरं घोरं बलेन महतावृतः .. .. 21 ..
तत्र विव्याध विशिखैः शार्दूलान्गवयान्मृगान् ..
रुरून्वराहान्महिषान्मृगेंद्रानपि भूरिशः .. 22 ..
स रथी मृगयासक्तो गहनं दंशित श्चरन् ..
कमपि ज्वलनाकारं निजघान निशाचरम् .. 23 ..
तस्यानुजः शुचाविष्टो दृष्ट्वा दूरे तिरोहितः ..
भ्रातरं निहतं दृष्ट्वा चिंतयामास चेतसा .. 24 ..
नन्वेष राजा दुर्द्धर्षो देवानां रक्षसामपि ..
छद्मनैव प्रजेतव्यो मम शत्रुर्न चान्यथा .. 25 ..
इति व्यवसितः पापो राक्षसो मनुजाकृतिः ..
आससाद नृपश्रेष्ठमुत्पात इव मूर्तिमान् .. 26 ..
तं विनम्राकृतिं दृष्ट्वा भृत्यतां कर्तुमागतम् ..
चक्रे महानसाध्यक्षमज्ञानात्स महीपतिः .. 27 ..
अथ तस्मिन्वने राजा किंचित्कालं विहृत्य सः ..
निवृत्तो मृगयां हित्वा स्वपुरीं पुनराययौ .. 28 ..
तस्य राजेंद्रमुख्यस्य मदयंतीतिनामतः ..
दमयन्ती नलस्येव विदिता वल्लभा सती .. 29 ..
एतस्मिन्समये राजा निमंत्र्य मुनिपुंगवम् ..
वशिष्ठं गृहमानिन्ये संप्राप्ते पितृवासरे .. 3.3.2.30 ..
रक्षसा सूदरूपेण संमिश्रितनरामिषम् ..
शाकामिषं पुरः क्षिप्तं दृष्ट्वा गुरुरथाब्रवीत् .. 31 ..
धिग्धिङ्नरामिषं राजं स्त्वयैतच्छद्मकारिणा ..
खलेनोपहृतं मेऽद्य अतो रक्षो भविष्यसि .. 32 ..
रक्षःकृतमविज्ञाय शप्त्वैवं स गुरुस्ततः ..
पुनर्विमृश्य तं शापं चकार द्वादशाब्दिकम् .. 33 ..
राजापि कोपितः प्राह यदिदं मे न चेष्टितम् ..
न ज्ञातं च वृथा शप्तो गुरुं चैव शपाम्यहम् .. 34 ..
इत्यपोंजलिनादाय गुरुं शप्तुं समुद्यतः ..
पतित्वा पादयोस्तस्य मदयन्ती न्यवारयत् ..35..
ततो निवृत्तः शापाच्च तस्या वचनगौरवात् ..
तत्याज पादयोरंभः पादौ कल्मषतां गतौ ..36..
कल्मषांघ्रिरिति ख्यातस्ततः प्रभृति पार्थिवः ..
बभूव गुरुशापेन राक्षसो वनगोचरः ..37..
स बिभ्रद्राक्षसं रूपं घोरं कालां तकोपमम् ..
चखाद विविधाञ्जंतून्मानुषादीन्वनेचरः ..38..
स कदाचिद्वने क्वापि रममाणौ किशोरकौ ..
अपश्यदंतकाकारो नवोढौ मुनिदंपती .. ..39..
राक्षसो मानुषाहारः किशोरमुनिनंदनम् ..
जग्धुं जग्राह शापार्तो व्याघ्रो मृगशिशुं यथा ..3.3.2.40..
रक्षोगृहीतं भर्तारं दृष्ट्वा भीताथ तत्प्रिया ..
उवाच करुणं बाला क्रंदंती भृशवेपिता .. 41 ..
भोभो मामा कृथाः पापं सूर्यवंशयशोधर ..
मदयंतीपतिस्त्वं हि राजेंद्रो न तु राक्षसः ..42..
न खाद मम भर्त्तारं प्राणात्प्रियतमं प्रभो ..
आर्त्तानां शरणार्त्तानां त्वमेव हि यतो गतिः .. 43 ..
पापानामिव संघातैः किं मे दुष्टैर्जडासुभिः ..
देहेन चातिभारेण विना भर्त्रा महात्मना .. 44 ..
मलीमसेन पापेन पांचभौतेन किं सुखम् ..
बालोयं वेदविच्छांतस्तपस्वी बहुशास्त्रवित् .. 45 ..
अतोऽस्य प्राणदानेन जगद्रक्षा त्वया कृता.
कृपां कुरु महाराज बालायां ब्राह्मणस्त्रियाम् .. 46 ..
3.3.m:
His heart was filled with compassion, his body with splendor, / and his feet with the rays of the crest-jewels of tributary kings. // 3.3.2.20
Once that lord of the earth, eager for the sport of hunting, / entered a terrible wilderness, surrounded by a large army. // 21
There with his arrows he pierced tigers, gavayas, deer, / ruru deer, boars, buffaloes, and also lions in abundance. // 22
Mounted on a chariot, devoted to the hunt, roaming the dense thicket fully armored, / he slew a night-stalker that possessed the form of blazing fire. // 23
His younger brother, overcome with grief upon seeing it, vanished into the distance; / seeing his brother slain, he reflected in his mind: // 24
“Indeed, this king is invincible even to the gods and the rakṣasas; / by trickery alone must my enemy be conquered, and not otherwise.” // 25
Having thus resolved, that evil rākṣasa in human form / approached the foremost of kings like an embodied calamity. // 26
Seeing him of humble bearing, arrived to offer his service, / the lord of the earth, out of ignorance, made him head of the kitchen. // 27
Then, having sported for some time in that forest, / the king ceased, abandoning the hunt, and returned to his own city. // 28
Of that foremost of mighty kings, a faithful wife named Madayantī / was renowned as beloved, just as Damayantī was to Nala. // 29
At that time the king, having invited the eminent sage / Vasiṣṭha when the day for the ancestors had arrived, brought him to his house. // 3.3.2.30
When the meat dish mixed with human flesh by the rakṣas in the form of the cook / was placed before him, the guru then spoke: // 31
“Fie, fie upon human flesh! O king, by you, a deceitful villain, / this has been offered to me today; therefore you shall become a rakṣas!” // 32
Not knowing it was done by a rakṣas, the guru, having thus cursed [him], / then reflected again and made that curse last for twelve years. // 33
Enraged, the king too said: “Since this was not done by me, / nor known, I have been cursed in vain; I too shall curse my guru!” // 34
Taking up water in his cupped hands and preparing to curse the guru, / Madayantī, falling at his feet, restrained him. // 35
Then, desisting from the curse out of respect for her words, / he dropped the water upon his feet; his two feet became blackened. // 36
From that time forth the ruler of the earth was renowned as Kalmāṣāṅghri; / by the curse of the guru, he became a forest-dwelling rākṣasa. // 37
Assuming a terrible rākṣasa form like the god of death at the end of time, / roaming the forest, he devoured various living beings, beginning with humans. // 38
Once in the forest, somewhere, resembling the god of death, he saw / a youthful, newly-wed sage couple making love. // 39
Feeding on humans, afflicted by the curse, the rākṣasa seized / the youthful son of the sage to devour him, as a tiger seizes a fawn. // 3.3.2.40
Seeing her husband seized by the rakṣas, his beloved, terrified, / weeping and trembling violently, the young woman said piteously: // 41
“Oh, oh, do not commit sin, upholder of the glory of the Solar dynasty! / You are indeed the husband of Madayantī, a lord of kings, not a rākṣasa. // 42
Do not devour my husband, dearer to me than life, O lord; / for you alone are the refuge of the distressed who seek protection! // 43
What use to me, like heaps of sins, are my vile, senseless life-breaths, / and this body, an excessive burden without my noble husband? // 44
What joy is there in this foul, sinful body made of the five elements? / This youth is a knower of the Veda, tranquil, an ascetic, learned in many scriptures. // 45
Therefore, by giving him life, protection of the world will be performed by you; / have mercy, O great king, upon a young brahmin woman! // 46 //”

3.3.s:

3.3.m:
great vows have been observed by me, subsisting on leaves, roots, and fruits.
All those do not bring me peace at any time.
Today the fruitfulness of my birth seems to have been attained,
since from the very darśana of you, my self has partaken of joy.
Seeking, one might sometimes attain one's desire after a multitude of years:'
even this popular saying has become true in my case,
at the rising and fruition of merits accumulated since birth,
since you, the protector of those who fear mundane existence, have become visible to my eyes.
From which land have you, the remover of the fear of worldly existence, come here?
I think you have come here, rested after travelling from afar;
as if having seen something exceedingly wondrous, you are delighted, judging from the radiance of your face.
You delight my mind, as if through conversing with love.
Today, for me who have committed a sin and have taken refuge in your lotus feet,
bring peace, O fortunate one, so that I may attain happiness."
Addressed thus by him, Gautama, an ocean of compassion,
properly prescribed the expiation for terrible sins.

3.3.m:
Gautama said:
"Well done, O king of kings! You are fortunate. Cast aside fear of great sins.
When Śiva is the protector of his devotees, where is the fear for those seeking refuge?
Hear, O noble king, of another celebrated sacred field,
the destroyer of great sins, delightful, called Gokarṇa,
where there is no persistence of sins, even the greatest of the great;
where Śiva, whose mere remembrance destroys all sins, is present.
Just as on the peak of Kailāsa, just as on the summit of Mandāra,
so the dwelling of Śambhu is established in the realm of Gokarṇa.
Not by fire, not by the moon, not by the lords of stars and planets,
is darkness completely dispelled, as it is by the sight of the sun;
even so, not by other sacred fords nor by delightful sacred fields,
can instantaneous purification from sin occur as it does from the darśana of Gokarṇa.
Even having committed a hundred sins such as the murder of a brahmin, a man
who enters Gokarṇa just once never fears sin anywhere.
There all the great-souled ones have attained peace through austerity.

3.3.m:
It is resorted to by Indra, Upendra, Viriñci, and others who desire perfections.
Whatever supreme vow is performed there even for a single day,
becomes equal to that performed elsewhere for a hundred thousand years.
Where, out of a desire for the welfare of the gods headed by Indra, Brahmā, and Viṣṇu,
the God is present in person under the name of Mahābala.
Obtained through terrible austerity by the rākṣasa named Rāvaṇa,
that liṅga was installed at Gokarṇa by the lord of gaṇas.
Indra, Brahmā, Mukunda, the Viśvedevas, the hosts of the Maruts,
the Ādityas, the Vasus, the two Aśvins, the Moon, and the Sun—
these gods, travelling in aerial chariots, together with their attendants,
attend upon the eastern gate of the God of gods who bears the trident.
Yama, Death himself in person, Citragupta, and Agni,
Together with the ancestors and the Rudras, have taken their place at the southern gate.
Varuṇa, the lord of rivers, along with the hosts of rivers headed by the Gaṅgā,
Serves Mahādeva, having taken his place at the western gate.
Likewise, Vāyu, Kubera, and Bhadrakarṇikā, the ruler of gods,

3.3.m:
Have taken their place at the northern gate together with the Mothers headed by Caṇḍikā.
Viśvāvasu, Citraratha, and the mighty Citrasena,
Along with the troops of gandharvas, worship Mahābala.
Rambhā, Ghṛtācī, Menā, Pūrvacitti, and Tilottamā—
Celestial women headed by Urvaśī dance before Śambhu.
Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa, Kaṇva, Viśvāmitra of great austerity,
Jaimini, Bharadvāja, Jābāli, Kratu, and Aṅgiras—
These and we, O king of kings, all spotless brahmin seers,
Worship the god Mahābala with devotion on all sides.
Atri together with Marīci, the lords of sages headed by Dakṣa,
And the great-souled ones headed by Sanaka sit and attend upon him.
Likewise sages, Sādhyas, wearers of deerskin garments,
Staff-bearers, those with shaven heads by vow, graduates, celibate students,
Their limbs reduced to mere skin and bone, their sins burned away by austerity,
Serve the god of gods, Pinākin, with supreme devotion.
Likewise gods with gandharvas, ancestors, siddhas, cāraṇas,

3.3.m:
Vidyādharas, kiṃpuruṣas, kinnaras, guhyakas, birds,
Nāgas, piśācas, vetālas, and mighty sons of Diti,
Endowed with various kinds of wealth, possessing various ornaments and mounts,
In aerial chariots resembling the sun, fire-colored, bright as the moon,
And others like masses of lightning, have surrounded him on every side.
They praise, sing aloud, recite, and bow down;
They dance and rejoice in Gokarṇa, O lord of the earth.
They obtain their desired objects and delight at their pleasure.
There is no sacred field equal to Gokarṇa in the entire globe of the cosmos.
There fierce austerity was practiced by the great-souled Agastya,
Likewise by Sanatkumāra, and by the sons of Priyavrata,
By Agni the foremost among gods, and by Kandarpa, O king,
Likewise by goddess Bhadrakālī, and by the wise Śiśumāra,
By Durmukha the lord of serpents, and the one named Maṇināga,
By nāgas headed by Ilāvarta, and by the mighty Garuḍa.
Even by the rākṣasa Rāvaṇa, and by the one named Kumbhakarṇa,

3.3.m:
And by the virtuous, great-souled Vibhīṣaṇa, austerity was practiced.
These and other gods, siddhas, dānavas, and humans,
Having worshiped Śiva, the lord of the god of gods, with devotion in Gokarṇa,
And having established thousands of liṅgas marked with their own names,
Attained supreme perfection and likewise made sacred fords.
Here are the shrines of all the gods, O king:
Of Viṣṇu the god of gods, of Brahmā the highest lord,
Of the heroic Kārttikeya, and of the elephant-faced one, O sinless one,
Of Dharma, of the guardian of the field, and of Durgā, O highly intelligent one.
In Gokarṇa there are tens of millions of Śivaliṅgas,
And countless sacred fords stand at every step.
What need is there of saying much here, O king? In Gokarṇa,
All stones are liṅgas, and all waters everywhere are sacred fords.
The greatness of the Śivaliṅgas and of the sacred fords in Gokarṇa
Is sung profusely by the great seers in the Purāṇas, O king.

3.3.m:
In Gokarṇa, the Koṭitīrtha has attained preeminence among sacred fords,
And Mahābala is the emperor of all Śivaliṅgas.
In the Kṛta age, Mahābala was white; in the Tretā age, extremely red;
In the Dvāpara age, of yellow color; and in the Kali age, he will be dark.
Though Mahābala pervades the seven netherworlds,
When the terrible Kali age arrives, he will assume tenderness.
Since the excellent sacred field of Gokarṇa, situated on the shore of the western ocean,
Burns away sins such as the killing of a brahmin, what is there to wonder at?
And here, those who are murderers of brahmins, those who harm living beings, the deceitful,
those devoid of all virtues, and those devoted to the wives of others,
those of bad conduct, those of evil ways, the ill-behaved, and the miserly,
the greedy, the cruel, the wicked, the foolish, thieves, and the excessively lustful—
they all, having reached Gokarṇa and bathed in the waters of the sacred fords,
and having beheld the god Mahābala, have gone to the abode of Śaṃkara.
There, on auspicious lunar days, under auspicious lunar mansions, on auspicious days of the week,

śivaliṃgaṃ bilvapatraṃ durlabhaṃ hi catuṣṭayam ..
aho balavatī māyā yayā śaivī mahātithiḥ .. 33 ..
nopoṣyate janairmūḍhairmahāmūkairiva trayī ..
upavāso jāgaraṇaṃ sannidhiḥ parameśituḥ .. 34 ..
3.3.d:
येऽर्चयंति महेशानं ते रुद्राः स्युर्न संशयः ..
यदा कदाचिद्गोकर्णं यो वा को वापि मानवः .. 27 ..
प्रविश्य पूजयेदीशं स गच्छेद्ब्रह्मणः पदम् ..
रवींदुसौम्यवारेषु यदा दर्शो भविष्यति .. 28 ..
तदा जलनिधौ स्नानं दानं च पितृतर्पणम् ..
शिवपूजा जपो होमो व्रतचर्या द्विजार्चनम् .. 29 ..
यत्किंचिद्वा कृतं कर्म तदनंतफलप्रदम् ..
व्यतीपातादियोगेषु रविसंक्रमणेषु च .. 3.3.2.130 ..
महाप्रदोषवेलासु शिव पूजा विमुक्तिदा ..
अथैकां ते प्रवक्ष्यामि तिथिं पार्थिव मुक्तिदाम् .. 31 ..
यस्यां किल महाव्याधो लेभे शंभोः परं पदम् ..
माघमासे महापुण्या या सा कृष्णचतुर्दशी .. 32 ..
शिवलिंगं बिल्वपत्रं दुर्लभं हि चतुष्टयम् ..
अहो बलवती माया यया शैवी महातिथिः .. 33 ..
नोपोष्यते जनैर्मूढैर्महामूकैरिव त्रयी ..
उपवासो जागरणं सन्निधिः परमेशितुः .. 34 ..
3.3.m:
those who worship the Great Lord become Rudras—there is no doubt.
Whenever any human being at all
enters Gokarṇa and worships the Lord, he goes to the abode of Brahmā.
When a new moon occurs on a Sunday, a Monday, or a Wednesday,
then bathing in the ocean, giving gifts, and offering libations to the ancestors,
worship of Śiva, silent recitation, fire sacrifice, observance of vows, and worshipping twice-borns—
whatever rite is performed yields endless reward.
During conjunctions such as Vyatīpāta, and during the sun's transits,
at the times of the great twilight worship, the worship of Śiva bestows liberation.
Now I shall tell you, O king, of one lunar day that bestows liberation,
upon which, indeed, the great hunter attained the supreme state of Śambhu:
in the month of Māgha, that greatly auspicious fourteenth day of the dark fortnight;
a Śiva-liṅga, and a bilva leaf—rare indeed is this group of four.
Ah, powerful is the illusion by which this great lunar day sacred to Śiva
is not kept with fasting by foolish people, just as the threefold Veda [is not studied] by the utterly mute!
Fasting, keeping vigil, and presence before the Supreme Lord—

3.3.s:
gokarṇaṃ śivalokasya nṛṇāṃ sopānapaddhatiḥ ..
śṛṇu rājannahamapi gokarṇā dadhunāgataḥ .. 135 ..
upāsyaināṃ śivatithiṃ vilokya ca mahotsavam ..
asyāṃ śivatithau sarve mahotsavadidṛkṣavaḥ .. 36 ..
āgatāḥ sarvadeśebhyaścāturvarṇā mahājanāḥ ..
striyo vṛddhāśca bālāśca caturāśramavāsinaḥ .. 37 ..
āgatya dṛṣṭvā deveśaṃ lebhire kṛtakṛtyatām ..
athāhamapyamī śiṣyā ṛṣayaśca tathā'pare .. 38 ..
rājarṣayaśca rājeṃdra sanakādyāḥ surarṣayaḥ ..
snātvā sarveṣu tīrtheṣu samupāsya mahābalam .. 39 ..
labdhvā ca janmasāphalyaṃ prayātāḥ sarvatodiśam ..
amunādya nareṃdreṇa janakena yiyakṣuṇā ..3.3.2.140 ..
nimaṃtrito'haṃ saṃprāpto gokarṇācchivamaṃdirāt ..
pratyāgamaṃ kimapyaṃga dṛṣṭvāścaryamahaṃ pathi ..
mahānaṃdena manasā kṛtārtho'smi mahīpate .. 141 ..
3.3.d:
गोकर्णं शिवलोकस्य नृणां सोपानपद्धतिः ..
शृणु राजन्नहमपि गोकर्णा दधुनागतः .. 135 ..
उपास्यैनां शिवतिथिं विलोक्य च महोत्सवम् ..
अस्यां शिवतिथौ सर्वे महोत्सवदिदृक्षवः .. 36 ..
आगताः सर्वदेशेभ्यश्चातुर्वर्णा महाजनाः ..
स्त्रियो वृद्धाश्च बालाश्च चतुराश्रमवासिनः .. 37 ..
आगत्य दृष्ट्वा देवेशं लेभिरे कृतकृत्यताम् ..
अथाहमप्यमी शिष्या ऋषयश्च तथाऽपरे .. 38 ..
राजर्षयश्च राजेंद्र सनकाद्याः सुरर्षयः ..
स्नात्वा सर्वेषु तीर्थेषु समुपास्य महाबलम् .. 39 ..
लब्ध्वा च जन्मसाफल्यं प्रयाताः सर्वतोदिशम् ..
अमुनाद्य नरेंद्रेण जनकेन यियक्षुणा ..3.3.2.140 ..
निमंत्रितोऽहं संप्राप्तो गोकर्णाच्छिवमंदिरात् ..
प्रत्यागमं किमप्यंग दृष्ट्वाश्चर्यमहं पथि ..
महानंदेन मनसा कृतार्थोऽस्मि महीपते .. 141 ..
3.3.m:
Gokarṇa is the stairway for men to the world of Śiva.
Listen, O king: I too have just now arrived from Gokarṇa,
having observed this lunar day of Śiva and having watched the great festival.
On this lunar day of Śiva, all wishing to see the great festival,
great multitudes belonging to all four varnas came from all countries;
women, the elderly, children, and dwellers in the four stages of life,
having come and seen the Lord of gods, attained fulfillment of purpose.
Then I too, these disciples, and other seers likewise,
and royal seers, O king of kings, and celestial seers headed by Sanaka,
having bathed in all the sacred fords and worshipped Mahābala,
and having attained the fruitfulness of our births, departed in every direction.
Having been invited today by this king, Janaka, who desires to perform a sacrifice,
I have arrived from Gokarṇa, the temple of Śiva.
On the way, my dear sir, having seen a certain wonder as I was returning,
with a mind filled with great joy, I am fulfilled, O protector of the earth.

3.3.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīye brahmottara khaṃḍe gokarṇamahimānuvarṇanaṃnāma dvitīyo'dhyāyaḥ .. 2 ..
3.3.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां तृतीये ब्रह्मोत्तर खंडे गोकर्णमहिमानुवर्णनंनाम द्वितीयोऽध्यायः .. 2 ..
3.3.m: Thus ends the second chapter, named 'Description of the Greatness of Gokarṇa', in the third Brahmottara section of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand verses.

3.3.s:
tatyajurgotrato dūraṃ gṛhītvā sakacagraham ..
saghaṭotsargamutsṛṣṭā sā nārī sarvabandhubhiḥ.. 48
3.3.d:
तत्यजुर्गोत्रतो दूरं गृहीत्वा सकचग्रहम् ..
सघटोत्सर्गमुत्सृष्टा सा नारी सर्वबन्धुभिः.. 48
3.3.m: cast her far away from their lineage, seizing her by her hair; / that woman was abandoned by all her relatives with the ritual expulsion of breaking a water-pot.

3.3.s:
vicaraṃtī ca śūdreṇa ramamāṇā ratipriyā ..
sā yayau strī bahiryāmā dṛṣṭā śūdreṇa kenacit .. 49 ..
3.3.d:
विचरंती च शूद्रेण रममाणा रतिप्रिया ..
सा ययौ स्त्री बहिर्यामा दृष्टा शूद्रेण केनचित् .. 49 ..
3.3.m: Wandering about, delighting in sexual pleasure, sports-loving, / that woman went out beyond the village boundary, and was seen by a certain śūdra.

3.3.s:
sa tāṃ dṛṣṭvā varārohām̐ pīnonnatapayodharām ..
gṛhaṃ nināya sāmnā ca vidhavāṃ śūdranāyakaḥ ..
sā nārī tasya mahiṣī bhūtvā tena divāniśam .. 3.3.3.50..
3.3.d:
स तां दृष्ट्वा वरारोहाम्̐ पीनोन्नतपयोधराम् ..
गृहं निनाय साम्ना च विधवां शूद्रनायकः ..
सा नारी तस्य महिषी भूत्वा तेन दिवानिशम् .. 3.3.3.50..
3.3.m: Seeing that woman of beautiful hips, with plump, prominent breasts, / that śūdra leader gently led the widow to his home. / That woman became his chief wife, and with him day and night,

3.3.s:
ramamāṇā kvaciddeśe nyavasadgṛhavallabhā ..
tatra sā piśitāhārā nityamāpītavāruṇī..51..
lebhe sutaṃ ca śūdreṇa ramamāṇā ratipriyā ..
kadācidbharttari kvāpi yāte pītasurā tu sā..52..
iyeṣa piśitāhāraṃ madirāmadavihvalā ..
atha meṣeṣu baddheṣu gobhiḥ saha bahirvraje .. 53 ..
3.3.d:
रममाणा क्वचिद्देशे न्यवसद्गृहवल्लभा ..
तत्र सा पिशिताहारा नित्यमापीतवारुणी..51..
लेभे सुतं च शूद्रेण रममाणा रतिप्रिया ..
कदाचिद्भर्त्तरि क्वापि याते पीतसुरा तु सा..52..
इयेष पिशिताहारं मदिरामदविह्वला ..
अथ मेषेषु बद्धेषु गोभिः सह बहिर्व्रजे .. 53 ..
3.3.m: delighting, the beloved mistress of the house lived in a certain place. / There, eating meat and constantly drinking liquor, / fond of pleasure, sporting with the śūdra, she bore a son. / Once, when her husband had gone somewhere, she, having drunk liquor / and distracted by the intoxication of spirits, desired to eat meat. / Then, while the sheep were tied together with the cows outside in the cattle pen,

3.3.s:
yayau kṛpāṇamādāya sā tamīṃdhe niśāmukhe ..
avimṛśya madāveśānmeṣabuddhyāmiṣapriyā .. 54 ..
3.3.d:
ययौ कृपाणमादाय सा तमींधे निशामुखे ..
अविमृश्य मदावेशान्मेषबुद्ध्यामिषप्रिया .. 54 ..
3.3.m: she went holding a sword, into the pitch darkness at the beginning of the night. / Craving meat, without thinking, in a fit of intoxication, mistaking it for a sheep,

3.3.s:
ekaṃ jaghānaṃ govatsaṃ krośaṃtaṃ niśi durbhagā ..
nihataṃ gṛhamānīya jñātvā govatsamaṃganā .. 55 ..
3.3.d:
एकं जघानं गोवत्सं क्रोशंतं निशि दुर्भगा ..
निहतं गृहमानीय ज्ञात्वा गोवत्समंगना .. 55 ..
3.3.m: the wretched woman killed a cow's calf that was crying out in the night. / Bringing the slain creature to the house, having realized it was a cow's calf, the woman,

3.3.s:
bhītā śivaśivetyāha kenacitpuṇyakarmaṇā ..
sā muhūrtamiti dhyātvā piśitāsavalālasā .. 56 ..
3.3.d:
भीता शिवशिवेत्याह केनचित्पुण्यकर्मणा ..
सा मुहूर्तमिति ध्यात्वा पिशितासवलालसा .. 56 ..
3.3.m: frightened, cried out 'Śiva! Śiva!' by virtue of some past meritorious deed. / Having reflected thus for a moment, craving meat and wine,

3.3.s:
chittvā tameva govatsaṃ cakārāhāramīpsitam ..
govatsārdhaśarīreṇa kṛtāhārātha sā punaḥ .. 57 ..
3.3.d:
छित्त्वा तमेव गोवत्सं चकाराहारमीप्सितम् ..
गोवत्सार्धशरीरेण कृताहाराथ सा पुनः .. 57 ..
3.3.m: she cut up that very cow's calf and made her desired meal. / Then, having made her meal with half of the calf's body,

3.3.s:
tadardhadehaṃ nikṣipya bahiścukrośa kaitavāt ..
aho vyāghreṇa bhagno'yaṃ jagdho govatsako vraje .. 58..
3.3.d:
तदर्धदेहं निक्षिप्य बहिश्चुक्रोश कैतवात् ..
अहो व्याघ्रेण भग्नोऽयं जग्धो गोवत्सको व्रजे .. 58..
3.3.m: she threw the [other] half of its body outside and deceitfully cried aloud: / 'Alas! This little cow's calf in the pen was torn apart and eaten by a tiger!'

3.3.s:
iti tasyāḥ samākraṃdaḥ sarvageheṣu śuśruve .
atha sarve śūdrajanāḥ samāgamyāṃtike sthitāḥ .. 59..
3.3.d:
इति तस्याः समाक्रंदः सर्वगेहेषु शुश्रुवे .
अथ सर्वे शूद्रजनाः समागम्यांतिके स्थिताः .. 59..
3.3.m: Thus her lamentation was heard in all the houses. / Then all the śūdra folk assembled and stood beside her.

3.3.s:
hataṃ govatsamālokya vyāghreṇeti śucaṃ yayuḥ ..
gateṣu teṣu sarveṣu vyuṣṭāyāṃ ca tato niśi .. 3.3.3.60 ..
3.3.d:
हतं गोवत्समालोक्य व्याघ्रेणेति शुचं ययुः ..
गतेषु तेषु सर्वेषु व्युष्टायां च ततो निशि .. 3.3.3.60 ..
3.3.m: Seeing that the cow's calf was slain by a tiger, they were filled with sorrow. / When they had all departed and the night was then spent,

3.3.s:
tadbhartā gṛhamāgatya dṛṣṭavāngṛhaviḍvaram .
evaṃ bahutithe kāle gate sā śūdvavallabhā .. 61 .
3.3.d:
तद्भर्ता गृहमागत्य दृष्टवान्गृहविड्वरम् .
एवं बहुतिथे काले गते सा शूद्ववल्लभा .. 61 .
3.3.m: her husband came home and saw the ruin of his household. / Thus, when much time had passed, that wife of the Śūdra,

3.3.s:
kālasya vaśamāpannā jagāma yamamaṃdiram .
yamopi dharmamālokya tasyāḥ karma ca paurvikam .. 62 ..
3.3.d:
कालस्य वशमापन्ना जगाम यममंदिरम् .
यमोपि धर्ममालोक्य तस्याः कर्म च पौर्विकम् .. 62 ..
3.3.m: falling into the power of Death, went to the abode of Yama. / And Yama, looking upon justice and her past deeds,

3.3.s:
nirvatrya nirayāvāsāñcakre caṃḍālajātikām ..
sāpi bhraṣṭā yamapurāccāṃḍālīgarbhamāśritā .. 63 ..
3.3.d:
निर्वत्र्य निरयावासाञ्चक्रे चंडालजातिकाम् ..
सापि भ्रष्टा यमपुराच्चांडालीगर्भमाश्रिता .. 63 ..
3.3.m: made her undergo hellish abodes and then assigned her to the Cāṇḍāla caste. / She too fell from the city of Yama and entered the womb of a Cāṇḍāla woman.

3.3.s:
tato babhūva jātyaṃdhā praśāṃtāṃgāramecakā ..
tatpitā kopi cāṃḍālo deśe kutracidāsthitaḥ .. 64 ..
3.3.d:
ततो बभूव जात्यंधा प्रशांतांगारमेचका ..
तत्पिता कोपि चांडालो देशे कुत्रचिदास्थितः .. 64 ..
3.3.m: She was then born blind from birth, black as an extinguished coal. / Her father was a certain Cāṇḍāla living somewhere in the country.

3.3.s:
tāṃ tādṛśīmapi sutāṃ kṛpayā paryapoṣayat ..
abhojyena kadannena śunā līḍhena pūtinā .. 65 ..
3.3.d:
तां तादृशीमपि सुतां कृपया पर्यपोषयत् ..
अभोज्येन कदन्नेन शुना लीढेन पूतिना .. 65 ..
3.3.m: Even though she was such a daughter, he nourished her with compassion, / with inedible, rotten, spoiled food licked by dogs,

3.3.s:
apeyaiśca rasairmātrā poṣitā sā dinedine ..
jātyaṃdhā sāpi kālena bālye kuṣṭharujārditā .. 66 ..
3.3.d:
अपेयैश्च रसैर्मात्रा पोषिता सा दिनेदिने ..
जात्यंधा सापि कालेन बाल्ये कुष्ठरुजार्दिता .. 66 ..
3.3.m: and with undrinkable broths she was nourished day by day by her mother. / Blind from birth, in time, while still a child, she was afflicted with leprosy.

3.3.s:
ūḍhā na kenacidvāpi cāṃḍālenātidurbhagā ..
atītabālye sā kāle vidhvastapitṛmātṛkā .. 67 ..
3.3.d:
ऊढा न केनचिद्वापि चांडालेनातिदुर्भगा ..
अतीतबाल्ये सा काले विध्वस्तपितृमातृका .. 67 ..
3.3.m: Extremely unfortunate, she was not married by any Cāṇḍāla. / When her childhood had passed, both her father and mother having died,

3.3.s:
durbhageti parityaktā baṃdhubhiśca sahodaraiḥ ..
tataḥ kṣudhārditā dīnā śocantī vigatekṣaṇā .. 68 ..
3.3.d:
दुर्भगेति परित्यक्ता बंधुभिश्च सहोदरैः ..
ततः क्षुधार्दिता दीना शोचन्ती विगतेक्षणा .. 68 ..
3.3.m: she was abandoned by her relatives and brothers as unfortunate. / Then, tormented by hunger, wretched, grieving, deprived of sight,

3.3.s:
gṛhītayaṣṭiḥ kṛcchreṇa saṃcacāla saloṣṭikā ..
pattaneṣvapi sarveṣu yācamānā dinedine .. 69 ..
3.3.d:
गृहीतयष्टिः कृच्छ्रेण संचचाल सलोष्टिका ..
पत्तनेष्वपि सर्वेषु याचमाना दिनेदिने .. 69 ..
3.3.m: taking a stick and a pebble, she moved about with difficulty. / Begging day after day in all the towns,

3.3.s:
cāṃḍālocchiṣṭapiṃḍena jaṭharāgnimatarpayat..
evaṃ kṛcchreṇa mahatā nītvā subahulaṃ vayaḥ .. 3.3.3.70 ..
jarayā grastasarvāṃgī duḥkhamāpa duratyayam ..
nirannapānavasanā sā kadācinmahājanān.. 71 ..
āyāsyaṃtyāṃ śivatithau gacchato bubudhe'dhvagān..
tasyāṃ tu devayātrāyāṃ deśadeśāṃtayāyinām .. 72 ..
viprāṇāṃ sāgnihotrāṇāṃ sastrīkāṇāṃ mahātmanām..
rājñāṃ ca sāvarodhānāṃ sahastirathavājinām .. 73 ..
saparīvāraghoṣāṇāṃ yānacchatrādiśobhinām ..
tathānyeṣāṃ ca viṭśūdrasaṃkīrṇānāṃ sahasraśaḥ .. 74 ..
hasatāṃ gāyatāṃ kvāpi nṛtyatāmatha dhāvatām ..
jighratāṃ pibatāṃ kāmādgacchatāṃ pratigarjatām .. 75 ...
saṃprayāṇe manuṣyāṇāṃ saṃbhramaḥ sumahānabhūt ..
iti sarveṣu gacchatsu gokarṇaṃ śivamaṃdiram .. 76 ..
paśyaṃti divijāḥ sarve vimānasthāḥ sakautukāḥ ..

Lacking food, drink, and clothing, she once learned of the crowds of people,
the travellers going forth as the auspicious lunar day of Śiva was approaching.
On that pilgrimage to the deity, of people journeying from various regions—
of high-minded brahmins accompanied by their wives and keeping their sacred fires,
of kings accompanied by their harems, with elephants, chariots, and horses,
with the clamour of their retinue, resplendent with vehicles, umbrellas, and the like,
and likewise of thousands of other mixed people, Vaiśyas and Śūdras,
laughing, singing, dancing somewhere, or running,
smelling, drinking at will, going forward, and shouting back and forth—
in that march of men there was immense bustle.
While all were thus going to Gokarna, the abode of Śiva,
all the gods seated in their aerial chariots watched with wonder.
Now this Cāṇḍāla woman too, out of longing for clothing and food,

Held by the hand of another woman, propelled by the deeds accumulated in her past life,
traveling for several days, she arrived at the sacred field of Gokarṇa.
Then, seated at a distance from the path with cupped hands opened,
begging repeatedly from the travellers, she spoke pitiful words:
‘Upon me, tormented for a long time by heaps of sins accumulated in past lives,
take pity, O people, by giving merely food!
O saviours of the deeply distressed, givers of supreme blessings,
doers of many merits, take pity, O people!

plunged in deep dust, take pity, O people!

whose whole body is burning, take pity, O people!

While the Cāṇḍāla woman was thus begging, into her outstretched hands
a certain most virtuous traveller cast a sprig of bilva leaves.
Feeling repeatedly that [cluster] which had fallen into her hands,
thinking it to be inedible, the afflicted woman threw it far away.
Cast off by her hand in the night, that sprig of bilva leaves,
by good fortune, fell upon the top of a certain Śiva liṅga.
Thus, on the night of Śiva’s fourteenth [lunar day], though begging repeatedly
from the travellers, she received nothing whatsoever by the turn of fate.
The night was spent by her there, behind Bhadrakālī,
at a place somewhat to the north, not very far—just halfway from it.
Then at dawn, her hopes dashed, overwhelmed by great sorrow,
the wretched woman slowly turned back, completely alone, toward her own land.

Then Śambhu, the Lord of the Universe, an ocean of the nectar of compassion,
commanded us with our aerial chariots: ‘Bring her here!’
This story of the cāṇḍāla woman has thus been narrated to you here;
likewise, Śambhu's compassion toward the wretched has been displayed.
Behold the fate that arises from the ripening of action, O high-minded one!
Even a base woman ascends to the supreme, disease-free station.
Because in a previous birth she gave no gift of food and the like,
she is tormented here by afflictions such as hunger and thirst.
Because, blinded by the rush of passion, she committed terrible sin,
by that action she became blind from birth in this very existence.
Because long ago, even knowing it, she ate a cow's calf,
by that action she became a despised cāṇḍāla woman here.
Because long ago she abandoned the noble path and indulged in the way of paramours,
by that sin, somehow or other, she became ill-behaved and unfortunate.
When long ago, as a widow intoxicated with passion, she embraced a paramour,

by that great sin she became afflicted with numerous leprous sores.
Because long ago, afflicted with desire, she copulated freely with a Śūdra,
by that sin she is tortured by profuse blood, pus, and worms.
She observed no good vows, nor did she perform sacrifices, charitable works, and the like;
deprived of all enjoyments, she is tormented by that sin.
Because in a previous birth she, bewildered, drank liquor,
by that sin she is tormented by the pangs of consumption and heart spasms.
In this very world, among all mortals, the signs of sin are completely
discerned, O tiger among sages, by great souls endowed with discernment.
Here, those who are stricken with many diseases, those who are bereft of sons and wealth,
and those who are afflicted with inauspicious marks, beggars destitute of shame,
deprived of clothing, food, drink, bedding, ornaments, ointments, and the like,
ill-favored, unlearned, crippled of limb, eaters of bad food,
those who are unfortunate and reviled, and others who serve outsiders—
all these were perpetrators of very great sins in a previous birth.
Deliberating thus with care, having observed the condition of people in the world,

3.3.m:
a wise man does not commit sin; if he should commit it, he is a slayer of himself.
This human body of a living being is the sole vessel for many actions;
one should always cultivate good action and constantly shun bad action.
One who desires happiness should perform merit; one who desires misery would practice sin.
When one of the two worlds is to be attained, a skillful person,
having resorted to this extremely rare human body,
who cares for his own welfare, should take refuge in the one God alone.
Moreover, even a man who continually commits all kinds of sins,
if his mind meditates upon Śiva alone, crosses over his wickedness.
When, having died in a previous birth, she reached the abode of Yama,
there arose a very great debate among the members of Yama's court:
"Although this was a brahmin woman, she corrupted the conduct of a noble family;
therefore, she has been brought here by us. Should she go to hell or not?
Was some little particle of merit performed by her in childhood or not?
Yet only after examining it thoroughly in this manner should punishment be imposed here, not otherwise.

3.3.m:
birth in a brahmin lineage is somehow obtained by men.
Therefore, she has no sin committed in earlier and earlier births;
otherwise, how could she attain birth in a noble family?
It is in this birth alone that an insurmountable sin was committed by her;
even so, she mostly does not deserve an abode in hell.
Moreover, having killed the calf of a cow, after reflecting, terror having seized her,
she uttered 'Śiva! Śiva!' through karma earned in a former birth.
If, for the destruction of sin, even once with devotion
she utters the greatly auspicious name of Śiva, then she would go to the supreme state.
Whatever is the fruit of this dread [sin] committed in a single birth,
let her experience it gradually by being born into a cāṇḍāla caste.
For what other hell is there for men in this world than this,
namely, constant torment by multitudes of numerous afflictions?
Birth in an evil family, poverty, severe disease, stupidity—
each one alone is a hell, or indeed all together, so what more [is needed]?"
Because of the burden of merit from a previous birth, she uttered his name when she was helpless.

3.3.m:
Through that, she will perform abundant merit in the end in another birth.
Having crossed over the torments of the flood of sins by that great merit,
led in the end by his attendants, she will attain the supreme abode.
We are not at all the rulers of such mortals.
Having deliberated himself, let the Lord himself do whatever is appropriate.
Thus in the city of the son of Vivasvat, having deliberated
with all [the ministers] led by Yama, Citragupta, and others, she was released and fell to the earth.
Because this woman, though unchaste, uttered the name of Śiva in the beginning, even by mistake,
through that merit she attained here again the virtue of worshipping Śambhu with bilva shoots.
Having fasted on Śiva's lunar day at holy Gokarṇa, upon the head of Śiva,
having kept vigil at night, she indeed performed the offering of bilva [leaves].
And whatever is the fruit of this merit performed without desire,
this very woman shall experience it this very day while you watch; [it is] not false.
Gautama said:
Having spoken thus, those messengers of Śiva, having drawn out
the particle of life from her cāṇḍāla womb, united it with divine splendor.

3.3.m:
Her, having entered a divine body, radiant as a mass of splendor,
those pleased servants of Śiva placed on an aerial chariot.
Then, endowed with supremely noble beauty and charm,
her limbs shining with celestial ornaments, wearing divine garments,
with a body possessing divine fragrance and radiating divine splendor,
adorned with garlands of celestial flowers, seated in the aerial chariot, she shone.
Amidst jeweled parasols, banners, and the sounds of singing and musical instruments,
that fair-faced woman rejoiced in the midst of Śiva's messengers.
Remembering again and again the births she had experienced,
frightened, trembling, having seen a profound marvel, she awoke as if from a dream:
“Who am I? Who are these great perfected beings? What is this delightful world?
Where has my miserable body born of the fierce cāṇḍāla clan gone?
Ah, what a great wonder has been seen, born of the play of illusion,
in that I have wandered again and again through thousands of births!
Ah, the astonishing māhātmya of the worship of Īśvara,
who, satisfied with a mere leaf, bestows his own abode!”

3.3.m:
Having placed her, who had thus attained detachment and was remembering the Lord's abode,
upon the celestial aerial chariot, those servants of Maheśvara,
while all the guardians of the worlds watched in wonder,
having taken leave, then brought her into the presence of Parameśvara.
O King, the exceedingly great marvel of the husband of the Mountain's Daughter has been told,
the māhātmya of a particle of devotion, which destroys the entire flood of sins.
The king said:
O Lord, what is the supreme world of Parameśa like?
Tell me its characteristics, if you have compassion for me.
Gautama said:
That bliss which is very difficult to attain even in the worlds of Brahmā and the lords of the gods,
where it exists eternally—that is the world of Parameśvara.
Where there is the transcendence of all things, where light is firmly established,
and where there is no contact with darkness anywhere—that is the world of Parameśvara.
Having crossed beyond the functioning of the qualities (guṇas), the yogins who have reached there
do not fall again, none of them—that is the world of Parameśvara.
Where anger, greed, intoxication, and the like do not dwell,

3.3.m:
and where the states such as birth do not exist—that is the world of Parameśvara.
That which is declared to be the sole field of all Vedic scriptures,
beyond which there is no higher treasure—that is the abode of Parameśvara.
By withdrawal of the senses, postures, meditation, control of the breath, and the like,
where yogins ever strive to attain by paths of yoga,
where the god, sporting together with the goddess whose form is
eternal bliss and spotless wisdom, abides—that is the world of Parameśvara.
By heaps of merit accumulated across many thousands of births,
the men and women who have ascended there sport in company,
fully absorbed in a mass of splendor that is inconceivable and delightful.
merged in the mass of splendor, incomprehensible and delightful, / they never perceive the division of day and night and the like.
That world of the supreme Lord is indeed hard to attain for the bad yogin.
It is reached only by those who are fully filled with devotion to him.
Those who rejoice in hearing and reciting his stories, who are friends to all beings, devoted solely to tranquility,

स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि मिथिलाधिपतेः पुरीम् .. 59 ..

श्रावयेद्वा जनो भक्त्या स याति परमां गतिम् .. 62 ..
3.3.m:
having crossed beyond the wheel of saṃsāra and cast off delusion, attain the abode of Śaṃkara and rejoice in bliss.
Therefore you too, O king of kings, go to Gokarṇa, the abode of Giriśa,
and, having quelled the flood of sins, attain the state of having fulfilled your purpose.
Bathing there at all times and worshipping Mahābala,
fasting attentively on Śivacaturdaśī,
keeping vigil at night and worshipping Śaṃkara with bilva leaves,
freed from all sins, you shall attain the world of Śiva.
This spotless counsel, O king, has been given to you by me.
May you have good fortune; I shall go to the city of the lord of Mithilā.
Having thus taken leave with affection, the sage Gautama went to Mithilā.
The king too, with a joyful mind, set out for Gokarṇa.
Seeing Mahādeva there, having bathed and worshipped Mahābala,
with the entire flood of sins shaken off, he attained the supreme abode of Śambhu.
Whoever constantly hears this charming Śaiva narrative,
or relates it with devotion, that person goes to the supreme state.

3.3.m:
Whoever, having faith, hears this narrative even once,
shall attain the world of Śiva together with the members of three times seven generations.
Thus has been told the complete, primeval seed of blessings, destroyer of the evils of hundreds of lives, which dispels the darkness of delusion,
the noble deed of the enemy of Manmatha, worthy of being sung by immortals, which should constantly be resorted to by fortunate people.
Thus ends the third chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of Śivacaturdaśī and Gokarṇa', in the Brahmottarakhaṇḍa of the third [section] of the glorious Skandamahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand verses.

3.3.m:
The king said:
What wonder did you see on the way, O brahmin, and where?
Tell me that, so that I may attain fulfillment of purpose.
Gautama said:
As I was coming from Gokarṇa, O ruler of subjects, in a certain place,
when midday arrived, I reached a clear lake.
Having sipped water there and dispelled the fatigue of the journey,
I resorted to a banyan tree with very glossy and cool shade.
Then, not far off, an outcaste woman, old, blind, emaciated in form,
with a drying face, without food, tormented by many diseases,
her body covered with leprous sores, swarming with rising broods of worms,
her hips clad in an old rag sticking with pus and blood,
distraught with the constriction of her throat caused by advanced consumption lodged in her neck,
her teeth lost, incoherent, rolling [on the ground] again and again,
sprinkled with harsh, hot dust touched by the fierce rays of the sun,
her limbs smeared with feces, urine, and pus, unapproachable because of the smell of blood,
with immense suffering as her pulse weakened under phlegm-disease and heavy panting,
with disheveled hair and limbs, nearing death—I saw [such a woman].
And beholding her in such agony, I was overcome with compassion;
waiting for her death, I remained right there for a moment.
Then I saw a divine aerial chariot brought by the attendants of Śiva,
as though sprinkling the path of the sky with rays of light.
In that aerial chariot, which was like a cage of the splendors of the sun, moon, and fire,
I saw attendants of Śiva resembling the sun.
They indeed held tridents, skull-topped staves, chisels, shields, and swords in their hands;
they were adorned with crescent moons and possessed the great brilliance of the dense moon and jasmine;
shining with crowns and earrings, radiant with bracelets of great serpents—
four followers of Śiva, endowed with auspicious marks, were seen by me.
Looking at them standing in the aerial chariot as they arrived, deeply amazed,
I approached swiftly, drew near, and asked those who stood in the sky:
"Obeisance, obeisance to you, best of the thirty gods, followers of the glorious feet of the Three-Eyed One!"

3.3.m: [Obeisance] to those carrying out the protection of the three worlds, who wield trident, shield, sword, and mace. / I have indeed recognized you as attendants of the feet of Maheśvara. / Is this journey of yours for the purpose of protecting the world, or born of sport? / Or have you undertaken an effort to overcome the flood of sins of all people? / Tell me out of compassion, for what purpose have you arrived here? / The messengers of Śiva said: / "Before us is seen this old cāṇḍāla woman, on the verge of death. / We have come to fetch her, commanded by the Lord." / When told this by those messengers of Śiva, I asked them yet again, / my mind overcome with astonishment, standing with folded hands: / "Ah, how does this terrible, most sinful cāṇḍāla woman deserve / to ascend a celestial aerial chariot, like a female dog [entering] a sacrificial arena? / Impure almost from birth, sinful, an adherent of sin, / how do you wish to lead this woman of wicked conduct to the realm of Śiva? / She has no knowledge of Śiva, no extremely severe austerity, / no truthfulness, no compassion—how do you wish to take her? / Feeding on the flesh of beasts, her belly filled with liquor, / constantly delighting in injuring living beings—how do you wish to take her? / Nor has she repeated the five-syllable mantra, nor performed worship of Śiva; / nor was the Lord Śambhu meditated upon—how do you wish to take her? / She observed no fast on Śiva’s lunar day, nor did she perform worship of Śiva; / she knows nothing of goodwill to living beings, nor offering of bilva leaves to Śiva, / nor Vedic sacrifices, charitable works, and the like—how do you wish to take her? / Neither has she bathed at sacred fords, nor given gifts, / nor undertaken vows—how do you wish to take her? / She ought to be avoided at the mere sight, not to mention in conversation; / destitute of the company of the good, fierce—how do you wish to take her? / Or is there any good deed of hers acquired in another birth? / Then why is she overcome by leprosy and worms? / Ah, this course of the Lord is incomprehensible to embodied beings, / when even sinful souls are taken to the supreme abode out of compassion!"

3.3.m: Thus addressed by me, those messengers of the God of gods, the trident-wielder, / dispelling all doubts, then answered me with affection. / The messengers of Śiva said: / "O brahmin, listen to a very great marvel, if you have curiosity, / regarding what you have now said concerning this cāṇḍāla woman. / In a previous birth she was a certain brahmin girl / named Sumitrā, whose face was like the full disk of the moon, / whose bodily characteristics were delicate like a garland of blooming jasmine, / the chaste daughter of a certain foremost brahmin of the Kaikeya country. / Seeing her growing up in her father's house, endowed with all auspicious marks / like a second embodiment of Rati, people were astonished. / Day by day she grew, pampered greatly by her relatives; / slowly she attained youth, like the great bow of the God of Love. / Then that young maiden was given according to rule by her father, / joined by his relatives, to a certain brahmin's son. / Having obtained a husband, possessing fresh youth, / of good conduct, she enjoyed herself for some time surrounded by relatives. / Then, through the power of time, her husband, afflicted by severe disease, / though endowed with beauty and youth, met his death, O sage. / When her husband died, being a chaste woman whose heart was burned with sorrow, / she lived for a few months well-behaved, with conquered senses. / Then, through the constantly developing burden of youth, / her heart became agitated by Kāmadeva. / Kept hidden by her circle of relatives, though instructed by the most eminent, / that woman was unable to restrain her mind, captivated by love. / Filled with intense desire, endowed with beauty and youth, / though a widow, she became especially devoted to the path of lovers. / Known by no one at all to be an unchaste woman, being clever, / that worst of women concealed her own misconduct for some time. / Overcome with pregnancy cravings, her breasts with thick, dark nipples, / in time even her circle of relatives realized she had been defiled by a paramour.

3.3.m: Sūta said: / Once again I shall speak of the supreme, wondrous glory of Śiva, / which destroys all sins for those who listen and releases them from the bonds of worldly existence. / For embodied beings drowning in the impassable ocean of wickedness, / no raft has been pointed out other than the worship of Śiva. / The wise man should always perform the worship of Śiva in this world; / if unable, he should view the worship that has been performed, his mind bowed with devotion. / Even one who performs the worship of Śiva, which grants liberation, without faith, / or merely views it, in course of time reaches the supreme abode. / In the Kirāta regions there was a king named Vimardana, / heroic, extremely unassailable, one who had conquered his enemies, and endowed with majesty. / Always addicted to hunting, stingy, pitiless, mighty, / an eater of all kinds of meat, cruel, surrounded by women of all castes. / Nevertheless, he constantly, without indolence, performed the worship of Śambhu, / especially on the fourteenth day of both the light and dark fortnights. / Having performed worship endowed with great magnificence, he rejoiced; / seized with great joy, he danced, praised, and sang. / As that all-devouring, ill-behaved king lived thus, / his queen was tormented by his conduct. / That queen, named Kumudvatī, who was endowed with good character and virtues, / once approached her husband in secret and asked him about it: / 'O king, this conduct of yours is a cause of great wonder! / Where is your great wicked conduct, and where is devotion to the supreme Lord? / You are always an omnivore, craving women of all sorts, / intent on all forms of violence, and cruel; how then do you have devotion to the Lord?' / Questioned thus, the king, having reflected for a long time, / knowing the three times, laughed and spoke to her, full of curiosity. / The king said: / 'In a previous life, O fair-faced one, I was a dog; / dwelling in the city of Pampā, I roamed about everywhere. / As time passed in this way in that best of cities, / I once went to a delightful temple of Śiva. / While worship was underway on that great tithi of the fourteenth day, / from afar, stationed at the outer gate, I watched the festival. / Then, chased by men with sticks in hand who were extremely angry, / I fled from that place, intent on saving my life. / Then, circumambulating the delightful temple of Śiva, / I reached the entrance again, and once again I was driven away. / Circumambulating that same temple of Śiva again, / out of greed for the balls of sacrificial food and the like, I approached the door once more. / Having thus made circumambulations there again and again, / while I sat in the entrance area, they struck me with sharp arrows. / With my limbs pierced, suddenly losing my life at the door of Śiva, / I was born into a line of kings through the power of Śiva's presence. / Because I witnessed the worship on the fourteenth day and looked upon the rows of lamps, / through that great merit, O lovely lady, I know the three times. / And due to the impressions of my previous birth, I am an omnivore and pitiless; / for the nature formed of past impressions is hard to overcome even for the wise. / Therefore on the fourteenth day I worship the Lord, the guru of the universe. / You too, O blessed one, worship the god Pinākin with faith.' / The queen said: / 'You know the three times, O king of kings, by the grace of the husband of Girijā; / you ought to tell me truly the story of my own previous birth.' / The king said: / 'In a previous life, you were a female pigeon flying in the sky; / somewhere or other, by chance, you obtained a piece of meat.

3.3.m: Then, having pursued you swiftly, that sharp-beaked bird / struck you down, caused you to fall, took the meat, and departed.

3.3.m: The queen said: / I have heard in full everything about my deeds in that previous birth, / and great wonder and devotion have arisen in my mind. / Now I wish to hear another thing, O wise one, knower of the three times: / Abandoning this body, what state shall we attain next?
