8 अथ सोमप्रदोषव्रतमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, तत्प्रसंगेनार्यावर्तस्थचित्रवर्मनृपतिकन्यायाः सीमन्तिन्या आख्यानवर्णनम्, तत्र तस्याः सीमन्तिन्याः स्वपितुः समीपे समा- गताभ्यां सामुद्रिकवेदिभ्यां ब्राह्मणाभ्यां सकाशादात्मनो भाविमहाभाग्यं भाविवैधव्यं च पृथक्पृथक्छ्रुत्वा वैधव्यप्राप्तिभीत्या मैत्रेय्याख्याया याज्ञवल्क्यमहर्षिपत्न्याः सकाशात्सौभाग्यवर्धनायोपायश्रवणार्थं शरणगमनम्, अम् तस्यै मैत्रेय्या सोमवारे शिवगौरीपूजनविधिकथनम्, अथ तया सीमन्तिन्या राजकन्यया मैत्रेय्यु- पदिष्टमार्गेण यथासांगसोमवारव्रतारम्भणम्, इन्द्रसेनपुत्रेण चित्राङ्गदेन सह सीमन्तिन्या विवाहः, अथ श्वशुरालये निवसतस्तस्य चित्राङ्गदस्य कदाचिद्यमुनां नदीं तर्तुं तरीमारूढस्य तर्या मध्येप्रवाहमकस्मान्निमज्जनम्, तर्यामारूढानां सर्वेषां मरणम्, तस्य चित्राङ्गदस्य राजपुत्रस्य तरीनिमज्जनेन मरणं विज्ञाय चित्र- वर्मादीनां शोककरणम्, एवं सीमन्तिन्या वैधव्यदशाप्राप्तिः, प्राप्तायामपि वैध- व्यदशायां सीमन्तिन्या यथावद्वर्षत्रयपर्यंतं सोमवारव्रतानुष्ठानकरणम्, अथ यमुनाजलेऽधोऽधो निमज्यमानस्य चित्राङ्गदस्य क्रीडन्तीभिर्नागकन्याभिः पाताले तक्षकपुरं प्रति नीत्वा तक्षकराजं प्रति निवेदनम्, तक्षकेण तस्य चित्राङ्गदस्य
सत्कारपूर्वकमुपास्यदेवताविषयकप्रश्नादिकरणम्, चित्रामगदेन स्वोपास्यभगव- च्छ्रीशङ्करभक्तिकथनम्, तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रसन्नेन तक्षकेण तस्य चित्राङ्गदस्य बहु- सत्कारकरणम्, ततश्चित्राङ्गदस्य स्वगेहं प्रति गंतुं प्रार्थनां श्रुत्वा तक्षकेण तं तत्र- त्यकल्पवृक्षरसान्नभोजनेनाप्याययित्वा बहुधनं दत्त्वा तथैकं राक्षसमेकं पन्नगं च साहाय्यार्थं दत्त्वा कामगममव्याहतगतिमश्वं च वाहनाय प्रदायाशीर्भिर- भियुज्य चित्रांगदस्य स्वसदनं प्रति गन्तुमाज्ञादानम्, ततश्चित्राङ्गदस्य तक्षकराजं प्रणम्याज्ञां गृहीत्वा हयमारुह्य धनं गृहीत्वा साहाय्यार्थं दत्ताभ्यां ताभ्यां राक्षसपन्नगाभ्यां सह ततः पातालात्प्रस्थाय यमुनाजलात्तूर्णमुन्मज्ज्य यमुनातीरे वाजिनमारुह्य विहारकरणम्, अथैतस्मिन्नेव समये स्वसखीभिः सह यमुनायां स्नातुमागतया सीमन्तिन्या तस्य दर्शनम्, ततः सखीमुखात्सीम- न्तिनीवृत्तान्तश्रवणं कृत्वा स्वयं तां सीमंतिनीं प्रति ऽअस्माभिस्तव पतिर्दृष्टस्त्वां प्रति स शीघ्रमेवागमिष्यति त्वं समाहितमना भव शोकं मा कार्षीर्वयं कामगमाः सिद्धानाम देवाः' इत्याश्वास्य तस्य चित्राङ्गदस्य स्वपितुर्नगरं प्रति गमनम्, तत्र नष्टपुत्रस्येन्द्रसेनस्य पितुर्दायादैः कृतं राज्यपदभ्रंशं श्रुत्वा चित्रांगदेन नागपुत्रद्वारा दायादान्प्रति राज्यपदत्यागाय संदेशप्रेषणम्, नागपुत्रप्रोक्तं चित्राङ्गदसदेशं श्रुत्वा सर्वैर्दायादैरिंद्रसेनाय राज्यपदं दत्त्वा पुत्रागमनवृत्तान्तं श्रावयित्वा निजापराधक्षमापणाय प्रार्थनां कृत्वा प्रसादनम्, ततश्चित्रांगदेन निजमंदिरं गत्वा स्वपित्रोर्वन्दनम्, पित्रोः पुत्रस्य प्राप्त्याऽत्यानन्दावाप्तिः, अथेन्द्रसेनेन राज्ञा निजपुत्रस्य पातालात्सुखागमनरूपमङ्गलमयवृत्तान्तनिवेदनाय चित्रवर्मनृपतिं प्रति दूतप्रेषणम्, दूतमुखान्निजजामात्रागमनवार्तां श्रुत्वा चित्रवर्मनृपतेरत्यानन्दमङ्गलावाप्तिः, ततो राज्ञा निजकन्यायै सीमन्तिन्यै सहर्ष तया पत्युर्मङ्गलमयवार्तानिवेदनम्, ततश्चित्रवर्मणेन्द्रसेनसुतं चित्राङ्गदं समाहूय पुनः सविस्तरविवाहविधिं विधाय तस्मै चित्रांगदाय निजकन्यायाः सीमन्तिन्या महता समारम्भेण प्रदानम्, अथ पातालानीतभूषणादिवस्तु- भिश्चित्रांगदेन स्वपत्न्याः संतोषकरणपूर्वकं तां समादाय स्वनगरीमागत्य महता'ऽनन्देन राज्यसुखोपभोगकरणम्, एवं सोमवारे शिवगौरीपूजन- व्रतप्रभावाच्चित्राङ्गदसीमन्तिन्योः सर्वाभीप्सितसुखावाप्तिवर्णनम्-. .... 187 2
3.3.m: 8. Now, the description of the māhātmya of the Somapradoṣa vow; in that context, the narration of the story of Sīmantinī, the daughter of King Citravarman in Āryāvarta. There, after Sīmantinī heard separately from two brahmins skilled in palmistry, who had approached her father, about her future great fortune and her future widowhood, and out of fear of attaining widowhood, her seeking refuge with the great sage Yājñavalkya's wife named Maitreyī to hear the means for enhancing her marital auspiciousness; Maitreyī's teaching her the rite of worshipping Śiva and Gaurī on Mondays; then, the royal maiden Sīmantinī's undertaking of the Monday vow with all its parts according to the path instructed by Maitreyī; the marriage of Sīmantinī with Indrasena's son Citrāṅgada; then, while residing in his father-in-law's house, Citrāṅgada's boarding a boat at one time to cross the Yamunā river, and the sudden sinking of the boat in the middle of the current; the death of everyone aboard the boat; King Citravarman and others mourning upon learning of the prince Citrāṅgada's death through the sinking of the boat; thus Sīmantinī's falling into the state of widowhood; even though the state of widowhood had befallen her, Sīmantinī's performing the observance of the Monday vow duly for a period of three years; then, as Citrāṅgada was sinking lower and lower in the waters of the Yamunā, sporting Nāga maidens taking him to Takṣaka's city in Pātāla and reporting him to King Takṣaka; Takṣaka's hospitably welcoming Citrāṅgada and asking questions about his chosen deity; Citrāṅgada's declaration of his devotion to the Lord, the venerable Śaṅkara, as his chosen deity; hearing his words, the pleased Takṣaka's showing great honor to Citrāṅgada; then, hearing Citrāṅgada's petition to go to his own home, Takṣaka's gratifying him by feeding him with dishes made from the elixir of the wishing-tree of that place, giving him vast wealth, granting a rākṣasa and a serpent for assistance, providing him with a horse capable of going anywhere at will with unobstructed gait for a mount, endowing him with blessings, and giving Citrāṅgada permission to go to his own residence; then, Citrāṅgada bowing to King Takṣaka, receiving his permission, mounting the horse, taking the wealth, departing from Pātāla together with the rākṣasa and serpent given for assistance, swiftly emerging from the waters of the Yamunā, and riding the horse in recreation along the bank of the Yamunā; now at that very time, Sīmantinī, who had come to bathe in the Yamunā with her companions, seeing him; then, hearing Sīmantinī's story from the mouth of her companion, Citrāṅgada himself saying to Sīmantinī, 'Your husband has been seen by us; he will return to you very soon; compose your mind and do not grieve; we are gods known as Siddhas who travel at will,' and thus comforting her, Citrāṅgada departing for his father's city; there, hearing that his father Indrasena, whose son was lost, had been deposed from his royal position by his kinsmen, Citrāṅgada sending a message to the kinsmen through the Nāga youth to relinquish the royal office; hearing Citrāṅgada's message spoken by the Nāga youth, all the kinsmen returning the royal office to Indrasena, reporting the news of his son's arrival, begging forgiveness for their transgression, and appeasing him; then, Citrāṅgada going to his own palace and bowing to his parents; the parents attaining supreme joy upon recovering their son; then, King Indrasena sending a messenger to King Citravarman to convey the auspicious news of his son's safe return from Pātāla; hearing the news of his son-in-law's arrival from the mouth of the messenger, King Citravarman attaining supreme joy and auspiciousness; then, the king joyfully conveying the auspicious news of her husband to his daughter Sīmantinī; then, Citravarman summoning Indrasena's son Citrāṅgada, performing the wedding rites again in full detail, and giving his daughter Sīmantinī to Citrāṅgada with great ceremony; then, Citrāṅgada pleasing his wife with ornaments and other articles brought from Pātāla, taking her, arriving at his own city, and enjoying royal happiness with great joy; thus, the description of Citrāṅgada and Sīmantinī obtaining all desired happiness through the power of the vow of worshipping Śiva and Gaurī on Mondays. .... 187 2

3.3.s: 9 atha sīmantinīkṛtasomavāravrataprabhāvakathanaprasaṅgena sumedhaḥ sāmavadākhyayordvayorveda- mitrasārasvatākhyabrāhmaṇadvayasya ṣutrayorvṛttāntavarṇanam, tatra sumedhaḥsāmavatorbrāhma- ṇaputrayorgurukule sāṃgavidyādhyayanānantaraṃ pitrājñayā nijavivāhārthaṃ dhanasaṃpādanāya vidarbhādhipateḥ samīpe gamanam, atha vidarbhādhipatinā yācamānau tau dvijasutau ni rīkṣya kiñcitprahasya-yuvāṃ dvayormadhya ekaṃ strīveṣeṇa veṣayitvā vipradaṃpatī bhūtvā sī- maṃtinyāḥ satkāramupalabhya matsamīpamāgacchataṃ tadāhaṃ yuvābhyāṃ bahu dhanaṃ dāsyāmi' ityukte sati rājājñāyā alaṃghanīyatāṃ manyamānābhyāṃ tābhyāṃ dvijakumārābhyāṃ sāmavantaṃ prati kṛtrimastrīveṣeṇa veṣayitvā dvijadaṃpatisvarūpeṇa naiṣadhadeśaṃ prati gamanam, tataśca somavāradine sīmantinyā tayormadhye puruṣasya mahādevabuddhyā striyāśca pārvatībuddhyā pūjākaraṇam, tayā sīmantinyā pārvatībuddhyā pūjitasya strīveṣadhāriṇaḥ sāmavadākhyasya dvijaputrasya tatkṣaṇameva satyatayā strītvaprāptiḥ, tataśca sīmantinīdattaṃ ratnasragvastrabhūṣaṇādi gṛhītvā prayātayordvijakumārayormadhye sāmavataḥ strītvaprāptyā kāmavikārotpattiḥ, tatastayā sāmavatyā jātayā kāmavihārārthaṃ sumedhasaḥ prārthanākaraṇam tataḥ sumedhasā nijamitrasya strītvaprāpti lakṣaṇairekānte svarūpeṇa ca dṛṣṭvā suratārthaṃ prārthayānāṃ tāṃ vivekavacanaiḥ kathaṃkāraṃ sāntvayitvā tāṃ sāmavatīṃ samādāya svagṛhaṃ samānīya svapitre tatpitre ca sarvavṛttāntanivedanam, atha śokākulābhyāṃ tatpitṛbhyāṃ tau nijaputrau samādāya vaidarbhabhūpaṃ prati gatvā tasmai 'tvaddoṣeṇa sāmavataḥ strītvaprāptiḥ' iti kathanam, tatastena mahībhṛtā tasya dvijaputrasya svītvanivṛttipūrvakapuṃstvaprāptaye bharadvājamunerupadeśena bharadvājamuninā tābhyāṃ dvijakumārābhyāṃ ca sahāmbikābhavanaṃ gatvā śrījagadambāyā upāsanākaraṇam, tatḥ prasannayā jagadambayā prādurbhūya svabhakta- kṛtasyānyathākartumaśakyatāṃ kathayitvā sāmavatyāḥ sumedhasā saha patnītvena kāmasukhopabhogārthamājñāṃ kṛtvā tatpituḥ sārasvatabrāhmaṇasya pūrvasutapekṣayā'dhika- guṇavatsuto bhaviṣyatīti varapradānam, tatastena sārasvatabrāhmaṇena tasyāḥ sāma- vatyākhyāyā nijasutāyāstasmai sumedhase vivāhavidhinā pradānakaraṇam, tayoḥ sumedhaḥsāmavatyorgārhasthyadharmasevanapūrvakaṃ kāmasukhopabhogakaraṇavarṇanam, itthaṃ sīmaṃtinīkṛtaśivabhaktimāhātmyavarṇanam ..... .... 191 2
3.3.d: 9 अथ सीमन्तिनीकृतसोमवारव्रतप्रभावकथनप्रसङ्गेन सुमेधः सामवदाख्ययोर्द्वयोर्वेद- मित्रसारस्वताख्यब्राह्मणद्वयस्य षुत्रयोर्वृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, तत्र सुमेधःसामवतोर्ब्राह्म- णपुत्रयोर्गुरुकुले सांगविद्याध्ययनानन्तरं पित्राज्ञया निजविवाहार्थं धनसंपादनाय विदर्भाधिपतेः समीपे गमनम्, अथ विदर्भाधिपतिना याचमानौ तौ द्विजसुतौ नि रीक्ष्य किञ्चित्प्रहस्य-युवां द्वयोर्मध्य एकं स्त्रीवेषेण वेषयित्वा विप्रदंपती भूत्वा सी- मंतिन्याः सत्कारमुपलभ्य मत्समीपमागच्छतं तदाहं युवाभ्यां बहु धनं दास्यामि' इत्युक्ते सति राजाज्ञाया अलंघनीयतां मन्यमानाभ्यां ताभ्यां द्विजकुमाराभ्यां सामवन्तं प्रति कृत्रिमस्त्रीवेषेण वेषयित्वा द्विजदंपतिस्वरूपेण नैषधदेशं प्रति गमनम्, ततश्च सोमवारदिने सीमन्तिन्या तयोर्मध्ये पुरुषस्य महादेवबुद्ध्या स्त्रियाश्च पार्वतीबुद्ध्या पूजाकरणम्, तया सीमन्तिन्या पार्वतीबुद्ध्या पूजितस्य स्त्रीवेषधारिणः सामवदाख्यस्य द्विजपुत्रस्य तत्क्षणमेव सत्यतया स्त्रीत्वप्राप्तिः, ततश्च सीमन्तिनीदत्तं रत्नस्रग्वस्त्रभूषणादि गृहीत्वा प्रयातयोर्द्विजकुमारयोर्मध्ये सामवतः स्त्रीत्वप्राप्त्या कामविकारोत्पत्तिः, ततस्तया सामवत्या जातया कामविहारार्थं सुमेधसः प्रार्थनाकरणम् ततः सुमेधसा निजमित्रस्य स्त्रीत्वप्राप्ति लक्षणैरेकान्ते स्वरूपेण च दृष्ट्वा सुरतार्थं प्रार्थयानां तां विवेकवचनैः कथंकारं सान्त्वयित्वा तां सामवतीं समादाय स्वगृहं समानीय स्वपित्रे तत्पित्रे च सर्ववृत्तान्तनिवेदनम्, अथ शोकाकुलाभ्यां तत्पितृभ्यां तौ निजपुत्रौ समादाय वैदर्भभूपं प्रति गत्वा तस्मै ऽत्वद्दोषेण सामवतः स्त्रीत्वप्राप्तिः' इति कथनम्, ततस्तेन महीभृता तस्य द्विजपुत्रस्य स्वीत्वनिवृत्तिपूर्वकपुंस्त्वप्राप्तये भरद्वाजमुनेरुपदेशेन भरद्वाजमुनिना ताभ्यां द्विजकुमाराभ्यां च सहाम्बिकाभवनं गत्वा श्रीजगदम्बाया उपासनाकरणम्, तत्ः प्रसन्नया जगदम्बया प्रादुर्भूय स्वभक्त- कृतस्यान्यथाकर्तुमशक्यतां कथयित्वा सामवत्याः सुमेधसा सह पत्नीत्वेन कामसुखोपभोगार्थमाज्ञां कृत्वा तत्पितुः सारस्वतब्राह्मणस्य पूर्वसुतपेक्षयाऽधिक- गुणवत्सुतो भविष्यतीति वरप्रदानम्, ततस्तेन सारस्वतब्राह्मणेन तस्याः साम- वत्याख्याया निजसुतायास्तस्मै सुमेधसे विवाहविधिना प्रदानकरणम्, तयोः सुमेधःसामवत्योर्गार्हस्थ्यधर्मसेवनपूर्वकं कामसुखोपभोगकरणवर्णनम्, इत्थं सीमंतिनीकृतशिवभक्तिमाहात्म्यवर्णनम् ..... .... 191 2
3.3.m: 9. Now, in the context of describing the efficacy of the Monday observance performed by Sīmantinī, the narration of the account of the two sons, named Sumedhas and Sāmavat, of two brahmins named Vedamitra and Sārasvata: / There, after completing the study of the sciences along with their auxiliary branches in the preceptor's home, the two brahmin sons, by their father's command, went before the ruler of Vidarbha to acquire wealth for their own marriages. / Then, having observed the two brahmin sons making their request and laughing slightly, the ruler of Vidarbha said: "Dress one of the two of you in a woman's attire, become a brahmin couple, receive Sīmantinī's hospitality, and come back to me; then I shall give you much wealth." When this was said, those two young brahmins, considering the king's command unavoidable, dressed Sāmavat in disguise as a woman and set out for the Naiṣadha country in the form of a brahmin couple. / And then, on a Monday, Sīmantinī performed worship of the male between the two with the mindset that he was Mahādeva, and of the woman with the mindset that she was Pārvatī. / For that brahmin son named Sāmavat, disguised in woman's attire and worshipped by Sīmantinī with the mindset that he was Pārvatī, femalehood was attained in reality at that very moment. / And then, when the two young brahmins had taken the jewels, garlands, garments, ornaments, and other gifts bestowed by Sīmantinī and departed, erotic longing arose in Sāmavat due to his transformation into a woman. / Then, she who had become Sāmavatī made a supplication to Sumedhas for erotic dalliance. / Then, in private, having observed by physical characteristics and actual form that his friend had attained femalehood, Sumedhas somehow consoled her with words of discernment as she begged for sexual union, took that Sāmavatī, brought her to his own home, and reported the entire story to his own father and to her father. / Then, distressed with grief, the two fathers took their two sons, went before the king of Vidarbha, and said to him: "Because of your fault, Sāmavat has attained femalehood." / Then, by the instruction of the sage Bharadvāja, so that the brahmin son might be relieved of femalehood and regain manhood, that king went together with the sage Bharadvāja and the two young brahmins to the abode of Ambikā and worshipped the glorious Mother of the Universe. / Thereupon, the pleased Mother of the Universe appeared, declared that what had been done by her devotee could not be undone, commanded that Sāmavatī should enjoy the pleasures of love as a wife with Sumedhas, and granted the boon that her father, the Sārasvata brahmin, would have a son endowed with even more virtues than the previous son. / Then, by that Sārasvata brahmin, his own child named Sāmavatī was given according to the rites of marriage to that Sumedhas. / The description of those two, Sumedhas and Sāmavatī, enjoying the pleasures of love while practicing the duties of householders; thus the narration of the glory of the devotion to Śiva performed by Sīmantinī. [Chapter] 191.

3.3.s:
10 atha śivamāhātmyavarṇanaprasaṃgenāvantīviṣayastha mandarāhvayabrāhmaṇavṛttāntavarṇanam, tatra tasya mandarākhyabrāhmaṇasya viṣayāsaktiparāyaṇatayā piṅgalākhyaveśyāsadmani nityaṃ nivāsakaraṇam, athaikadā tasyā veśyāyāḥ sadmani tasmindvije nivasati sati dharmātmana ṛṣabhanāmnaḥ śivayogina āgamanam, tasyarṣabhayoginastābhyāṃ mandaradvijapiṃgalāveśyābhyāṃ pādaprakṣālanādipādasaṃvāhanāntasamyakchuśrūṣākaraṇenai- karātraparyaṃtamatisantoṣasamutpādanam, atha dvitīye'hni yātrāprasaṃgenāgatasya tasya- rṣabhayogino gamanam, tataḥ kālāntareṇa mandaradvijasya maraṇānantaraṃ daśārṇādhi- patervajrabāhorbhūpālasya bhāryāyāṃ janma, tatrādau garbhāvasthāyāmeva tasyā nṛpabhāryāyā maraṇārthaṃ sapatnībhiśchadmanā viṣe datte'pi daivayogānna maraṇam, paraṃtu viṣajanyadā- hādatyantakleśāvāptiḥ, tasyāṃ nṛpabhāryāyāṃ samutpannasya bālakasya viṣotpannadāhe- nātikleśaprāptiḥ, ubhayorapi mātāputrayorgarayogaprabhāveṇātikleśaṃ samavekṣya rājñā vaidyadvārā bheṣaje kṛte'pyasvāsthyaṃ dṛṣṭvā ' nūnametau narakādāgatau ' iti svabuddhyā niścitya nijasārathidvārā rathena vijaneraṇye tayoḥ parityāgakaraṇam ,atha tena śiśunā bālakena saha vane vicaraṃtyā tayā rājyapatnyā daivayogātsudūre labdhena vaṇik mārgeṇa vaiśyanagaraṃ prati gamanam, atha tannagarasvāminaḥ padmākarākhyavaiśyasya dāsyā
tāṃ nṛpāganāṃ viditvā svasvāminaḥ padmākaravaiśyasya samīpe tasyānayana, tataḥ padmākaravaiśyena tasyā rājapatnyāḥ sāṃtvanaṃ kṛtvā satkārapūrvakaṃ svagṛhe sthāpanam, atha tatra vaiśyasadmani tasyāṃ rājapatnyāṃ nivasantyāṃ satyāṃ kadāciddaivayogena tasyā bālakasya vraṇādirogeṇa maraṇam, tadānīṃ tayā rājapatnyātivilāpakaraṇam, daiva- yogāttasminneva dine tasyaiva padmākaravaiśyasya gṛhe pūrvoktasyarṣabhākhyaśivayogino yātrāprasaṃgenāgamanam, tenarṣabhaśivayoginā vaiśyakṛtaṃ pūjāsatkāraṃ gṛhītvā putra- maraṇena bhṛśaṃ śocantyāstasyā rājapatnyāḥ samīpaṃ gatvā tāṃ prati paramārthayodhopadeśena śivabhaktikaraṇāyājñākaraṇapūrvakaṃ tasyā mṛtasya putrasya samīpaṃ gatvā śivamantrābhimantritabhasmanā tasya prāṇasaṃjīvanakaraṇam, tato bālake saṃjīvite sati rājñyāḥ sarvajanānāṃ cātyānandaprāptiḥ, tata ṛṣabhaśivayoginā tayormātāputrayordehayoḥ śivamantrābhimantritena bhasmanā sparśanam, tadbhasmasparśamātreṇa tayo- rmātāputrayordivyadehatvaprāptiḥ, tatastasya bālakasyarṣabhaśivayoginā bhadrāyuriti nāmakaraṇapūrvakamubhayorapi bhāvibhāgyodayaṃ varṇayitvā śiśorvidyāprāptiparyantaṃ padmākaravaiśyasya gṛhe nivāsāyājñāṃ kṛtvā yātrākaraṇārthaṃ sthānāṃtaraṃ prati gamanama 193 2.
3.3.d:
10 अथ शिवमाहात्म्यवर्णनप्रसंगेनावन्तीविषयस्थ मन्दराह्वयब्राह्मणवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, तत्र तस्य मन्दराख्यब्राह्मणस्य विषयासक्तिपरायणतया पिङ्गलाख्यवेश्यासद्मनि नित्यं निवासकरणम्, अथैकदा तस्या वेश्यायाः सद्मनि तस्मिन्द्विजे निवसति सति धर्मात्मन ऋषभनाम्नः शिवयोगिन आगमनम्, तस्यर्षभयोगिनस्ताभ्यां मन्दरद्विजपिंगलावेश्याभ्यां पादप्रक्षालनादिपादसंवाहनान्तसम्यक्छुश्रूषाकरणेनै- करात्रपर्यंतमतिसन्तोषसमुत्पादनम्, अथ द्वितीयेऽह्नि यात्राप्रसंगेनागतस्य तस्य- र्षभयोगिनो गमनम्, ततः कालान्तरेण मन्दरद्विजस्य मरणानन्तरं दशार्णाधि- पतेर्वज्रबाहोर्भूपालस्य भार्यायां जन्म, तत्रादौ गर्भावस्थायामेव तस्या नृपभार्याया मरणार्थं सपत्नीभिश्छद्मना विषे दत्तेऽपि दैवयोगान्न मरणम्, परंतु विषजन्यदा- हादत्यन्तक्लेशावाप्तिः, तस्यां नृपभार्यायां समुत्पन्नस्य बालकस्य विषोत्पन्नदाहे- नातिक्लेशप्राप्तिः, उभयोरपि मातापुत्रयोर्गरयोगप्रभावेणातिक्लेशं समवेक्ष्य राज्ञा वैद्यद्वारा भेषजे कृतेऽप्यस्वास्थ्यं दृष्ट्वा ' नूनमेतौ नरकादागतौ ' इति स्वबुद्ध्या निश्चित्य निजसारथिद्वारा रथेन विजनेरण्ये तयोः परित्यागकरणम् ,अथ तेन शिशुना बालकेन सह वने विचरंत्या तया राज्यपत्न्या दैवयोगात्सुदूरे लब्धेन वणिक् मार्गेण वैश्यनगरं प्रति गमनम्, अथ तन्नगरस्वामिनः पद्माकराख्यवैश्यस्य दास्या
तां नृपागनां विदित्वा स्वस्वामिनः पद्माकरवैश्यस्य समीपे तस्यानयन, ततः पद्माकरवैश्येन तस्या राजपत्न्याः सांत्वनं कृत्वा सत्कारपूर्वकं स्वगृहे स्थापनम्, अथ तत्र वैश्यसद्मनि तस्यां राजपत्न्यां निवसन्त्यां सत्यां कदाचिद्दैवयोगेन तस्या बालकस्य व्रणादिरोगेण मरणम्, तदानीं तया राजपत्न्यातिविलापकरणम्, दैव- योगात्तस्मिन्नेव दिने तस्यैव पद्माकरवैश्यस्य गृहे पूर्वोक्तस्यर्षभाख्यशिवयोगिनो यात्राप्रसंगेनागमनम्, तेनर्षभशिवयोगिना वैश्यकृतं पूजासत्कारं गृहीत्वा पुत्र- मरणेन भृशं शोचन्त्यास्तस्या राजपत्न्याः समीपं गत्वा तां प्रति परमार्थयोधोपदेशेन शिवभक्तिकरणायाज्ञाकरणपूर्वकं तस्या मृतस्य पुत्रस्य समीपं गत्वा शिवमन्त्राभिमन्त्रितभस्मना तस्य प्राणसंजीवनकरणम्, ततो बालके संजीविते सति राज्ञ्याः सर्वजनानां चात्यानन्दप्राप्तिः, तत ऋषभशिवयोगिना तयोर्मातापुत्रयोर्देहयोः शिवमन्त्राभिमन्त्रितेन भस्मना स्पर्शनम्, तद्भस्मस्पर्शमात्रेण तयो- र्मातापुत्रयोर्दिव्यदेहत्वप्राप्तिः, ततस्तस्य बालकस्यर्षभशिवयोगिना भद्रायुरिति नामकरणपूर्वकमुभयोरपि भाविभाग्योदयं वर्णयित्वा शिशोर्विद्याप्राप्तिपर्यन्तं पद्माकरवैश्यस्य गृहे निवासायाज्ञां कृत्वा यात्राकरणार्थं स्थानांतरं प्रति गमनम 193 2.
3.3.m: 10. Now, in the context of describing the māhātmya of Śiva, the narrative of the brahmin named Mandara residing in the region of Avanti is described. There, because of that brahmin named Mandara being devoted to attachment to sensual pleasures, he continuously dwelled in the house of a courtesan named Piṅgalā. Then, once while that twice-born was dwelling in that courtesan's house, the arrival of a Śaiva ascetic named Ṛṣabha, whose self was righteousness, [occurred]. By both the brahmin Mandara and the courtesan Piṅgalā performing proper service for that ascetic Ṛṣabha, beginning with washing his feet and ending with massaging his feet, great satisfaction was produced [in him] for the duration of a single night. Then on the second day, that ascetic Ṛṣabha, who had arrived in the course of a pilgrimage, departed. Later, after the death of the brahmin Mandara in the course of time, his birth in the wife of King Vajrabāhu, the sovereign of Daśārṇa, [took place]. There, right at the stage of being in the womb, although poison was given in secret by the co-wives for the purpose of killing that king's wife, by the arrangement of destiny death did not occur; however, from the burning caused by the poison, extreme distress was obtained. Extreme distress was obtained by the burning caused by the poison in the young boy who was born to that king's wife. Seeing the extreme distress of both mother and child through the effect of the contact with poison, though medicine was administered through physicians by the king, seeing their indisposition, having resolved in his mind, "Surely these two have come from hell," he had them abandoned in a desolate wilderness by his chariot-driver in a chariot. Then, wandering in the forest with that infant boy, the king's wife, by the arrangement of destiny, went along a merchants' route found far away toward a city of vaiśyas. Then, through a female servant of the lord of that city, a vaiśya named Padmākara, upon recognizing that queen, she was brought to the presence of her master, the vaiśya Padmākara. Then, after the vaiśya Padmākara comforted that king's wife, he settled her with honor in his own house. Then, while that king's wife was living there in the vaiśya's house, by the turn of fate the death of that young boy occurred through an affliction of boils and other diseases. Then the king's wife wailed intensely. By the turn of fate on that very day, in the house of that very vaiśya Padmākara, the arrival of the previously mentioned Śaiva ascetic named Ṛṣabha took place in the course of a pilgrimage. That Śaiva ascetic Ṛṣabha, having received the worshipful reception done by the vaiśya, approached that king's wife who was grieving severely on account of the death of her son; and, having instructed her with the teaching of the supreme truth to practice devotion to Śiva, he approached that dead son of hers and revived his life-breath by means of sacred ash consecrated with Śiva mantras. Then, upon the boy being revived, extreme joy was obtained by the queen and by all the people. Then the Śaiva ascetic Ṛṣabha touched the bodies of both mother and son with sacred ash consecrated with Śiva mantras. Merely by the touch of that sacred ash, divine bodies were attained by both mother and son. Then the Śaiva ascetic Ṛṣabha gave that boy the name Bhadrāyus, described the future rise of fortune for both, ordered [them] to reside in the house of the vaiśya Padmākara until the acquisition of learning for the child, and departed for another place to continue his pilgrimage. 193 2.

3.3.s:
11 atha piṅgalāveśyāyāḥ śrīśivabhaktarṣabhākhyaśivayogipūjanasatkāraprabhāveṇa janmā- ntare citrāṅgadarājapatnyāṃ sīmantinyākhyāyāṃ janmavarṇanam, atha bhadrāyoḥ padmākaravaiśyagṛhe tasya padmākaravaiśyasya putreṇa sunayena saha bālyattaḥ sakhyapūrvakaṃ vṛddhiḥ sahakrīḍādikaṃ ca, atha tayorvaiśyakumārarājakumārayoḥ padmākaravaiśyena brāhma- ṇadvāropanayanādisaṃskārakaraṇapūrvakavidyādhyayanasaṃpannatākaraṇam, atha bhadrāyo rājakumārasya ṣoḍaśe varṣe saṃprāpte tatsamīpe pūrvoktasyarṣabhayogīśasyāgamanam, tasya- rṣabhayogino bhadrāyumātrā svaputreṇa saha vandanakaraṇaṃ bhadrāyoḥ sanmārgopadeśāya prārthanākaraṇaṃ ca, tata ṛṣabhaśivayoginā bhadrāyuṣe rājaputrāya śrutismṛtipurāṇaprokta sanātanavarṇāśramānurūpadharmopadeśakaraṇam, atha sarvasaṃkaṭavimuktaye śrīśivasevo-
padeśakaraṇam...... 195 2
3.3.d:
11 अथ पिङ्गलावेश्यायाः श्रीशिवभक्तर्षभाख्यशिवयोगिपूजनसत्कारप्रभावेण जन्मा- न्तरे चित्राङ्गदराजपत्न्यां सीमन्तिन्याख्यायां जन्मवर्णनम्, अथ भद्रायोः पद्माकरवैश्यगृहे तस्य पद्माकरवैश्यस्य पुत्रेण सुनयेन सह बाल्यत्तः सख्यपूर्वकं वृद्धिः सहक्रीडादिकं च, अथ तयोर्वैश्यकुमारराजकुमारयोः पद्माकरवैश्येन ब्राह्म- णद्वारोपनयनादिसंस्कारकरणपूर्वकविद्याध्ययनसंपन्नताकरणम्, अथ भद्रायो राजकुमारस्य षोडशे वर्षे संप्राप्ते तत्समीपे पूर्वोक्तस्यर्षभयोगीशस्यागमनम्, तस्य- र्षभयोगिनो भद्रायुमात्रा स्वपुत्रेण सह वन्दनकरणं भद्रायोः सन्मार्गोपदेशाय प्रार्थनाकरणं च, तत ऋषभशिवयोगिना भद्रायुषे राजपुत्राय श्रुतिस्मृतिपुराणप्रोक्त सनातनवर्णाश्रमानुरूपधर्मोपदेशकरणम्, अथ सर्वसंकटविमुक्तये श्रीशिवसेवो-
पदेशकरणम्...... 195 2
3.3.m: 11. Now, the description of the courtesan Piṅgalā's birth, through the power of her worship and reception of the Śaiva ascetic named Ṛṣabha who was a devotee of Śiva, in another birth as Sīmantinī, the queen of King Citrāṅgada; then the growth of Bhadrāyus in the house of the vaiśya Padmākara alongside the son of that vaiśya Padmākara, named Sunaya, with friendship from childhood, playing together and the like; then the vaiśya Padmākara having the sacred rites such as the investiture of the sacred thread performed for those two, the vaiśya youth and the prince, by brahmins, and bringing about their mastery of study; then, upon the prince Bhadrāyus reaching his sixteenth year, the arrival of that previously mentioned lord of ascetics Ṛṣabha near him; the bowing performed by the mother of Bhadrāyus along with her son to that ascetic Ṛṣabha and her prayer to instruct Bhadrāyus in the righteous path; then the Śaiva ascetic Ṛṣabha giving instruction in the eternal duty appropriate to caste and life-stage proclaimed in the Vedas, smṛtis, and Purāṇas to Prince Bhadrāyus; then his instructing in the service of glorious Śiva for liberation from all distress. 195 2.

3.3.s:
12 atha śrīmatarṣabhaśivayoginā sarvarakṣākaraśrīśivakavacastotropadeśaṃ kṛtvā tasmai bhadrā-
yunāmne rājaputrāya vijayakaraṃ sarvaśatruvināśakaṃ śaṃkhaṃ pradāya śivamantramantritena
bhasmanā tadaṃgaṃ spṛṣṭvā tasmai dvādaśasahasragajabalaṃ dattvā darśanamātrācchatruvijayakaraṃ
khaṅgaṃ pradāya karaṇīyakṛtyopadeśaṃ kṛtvā śubhāśīrvacanena samanuśāsya tābhyāṃ pūjā-
satkāramavāpyābhīṣṭadeśaṃ prati gamanam..... 196 2
3.3.d:
12 अथ श्रीमतर्षभशिवयोगिना सर्वरक्षाकरश्रीशिवकवचस्तोत्रोपदेशं कृत्वा तस्मै भद्रा-
युनाम्ने राजपुत्राय विजयकरं सर्वशत्रुविनाशकं शंखं प्रदाय शिवमन्त्रमन्त्रितेन
भस्मना तदंगं स्पृष्ट्वा तस्मै द्वादशसहस्रगजबलं दत्त्वा दर्शनमात्राच्छत्रुविजयकरं
खङ्गं प्रदाय करणीयकृत्योपदेशं कृत्वा शुभाशीर्वचनेन समनुशास्य ताभ्यां पूजा-
सत्कारमवाप्याभीष्टदेशं प्रति गमनम्..... 196 2
3.3.m: 12. Now, the illustrious Śaiva ascetic Ṛṣabha, having given instruction in the glorious Śivakavaca hymn that affords all protection, gave to that prince named Bhadrāyus a conch that grants victory and destroys all enemies, touched his body with sacred ash consecrated with Śiva mantras, bestowed upon him the strength of twelve thousand elephants, gave a sword that grants victory over enemies merely by its sight, instructed him on duties to be performed, directed him with words of auspicious blessing, and, having received worshipful reception from both of them, departed to his desired destination. 196 2.

3.3.s:
13 atha tataḥ kadācitsvalpīyasaiva samayena tasya śivabhaktiṃ prakurvato bhadrāyoḥ
piturvajrabāhunāmakasya daśārṇadeśabhūpālasya śatruṇā magadharājena mahatā sainyena saha yuddhāyāgamanam, tato magadharājena daśārṇadeśabhūpena saha yuddhaṃ kṛtvā yuddhe taṃ nirjitya tasya sarvaṃ sainyaṃ nirṇāśya daśārṇadeśarāṣṭraṃ svāyattīkṛtya taṃ rathe baddhvā svadeśaṃ prati gamanam, itthaṃ vaiśyanagare nivasatā bhadrāyurājaputreṇa janamukhānnija-
pitṛrāṣṭraviplavavārtāṃ śrutvā padmākaravaiśyaputreṇa sunayena sahāyena hayamadhiruhya mahatā javena nijapitṛpālitaṃ daśārṇadeśaṃ magadheśvarākhyaśatrubhūpasainikairvidhvastaṃ nirīkṣya tataḥ krodhāveśena tūrṇameva śatrusenāṃ praviśya śivayogidattavijayaśaṃkhamādhmāya vijayakhaḍgaṃ codyamya sarvāñchatrugaṇānmūrcchanayā vimohya bahuśaḥ śatrūnhatvā śatrubhī rathe nibaddhasyātmanaḥ piturbandhānmokṣayitvā śatruvaśagāḥ sarvāḥ svapitṛpatnīḥ puravāsijanānāṃ patnīśca kanyāśca godhanādīni ca mocayitvā svapitrādīnsarvānāśvāsya svapuryāṃ saṃpreṣaṇam, tato'risainye praveśaṃ kṛtvā teṣāṃ strīgajāśvarathadāsadāsyādisarvasaṃpattiṃ hṛtvā magadheśaṃ parājitya samantryādiparijanaṃ taṃ nirbadhya ca svapurīṃ pratyāgamanam, atha tena bhadrāyunā suvyaktasvanāmādyakathayitvaiva
sāmānyataḥ kṣatriyaputratvakathanapūrvakaṃ svapituḥ pādābhivandanakaraṇam, atha piturnamanānaṃtaraṃ tena sunayākhyena vaiśyaputreṇa saha bhadrāyuṇā vaiśyapuraṃ pratyāgatya nijamātre tasmai padmākarākhyāya vaiśyavaryāya ca sarvayuddhādivṛttāntanivedanam, atha dvitīye'hni candrāṃgadāparaparyāyaṃ citrāṅgadaṃ nṛpaṃ prati tasya pūrvoktasyarṣa- bhākhyaśivayogina āgamanaṃ citrāṃgadaṃ prati bhadrāyuṣe rājaputrāya kanyāpradā- nārthamupadeśapūrvakamājñākaraṇaṃ ca, tata ṛṣabhayogivacanāccitrāṅgadena bhūpena bhadrā- yuṣamāhūya tasmai kīrtimālinyākhyāṃ nijakanyāṃ pradāya vaivāhikavidhikaraṇāya samārambhakaraṇam, atha tatpiturvajrabāhoḥ samīpe dūtaṃ preṣayitvā putrasyodvāhārthaṃ satkārapūrvakaṃ nimantraṇam, vajrabāhoḥ saparivārasya tatra niṣadheśarājadhānyāmāga- manam, tasyāgatasya piturvajravāhorbhadrāyunā putreṇābhivādanam, tathāpyavijñātatatku- lanāmnā vajrabāhunā tasya bhadrāyorjijñāsayā praśne kṛte sati niṣadheśvareṇa vajrabāhuṃ prati 'ayaṃ tvayā mātrā saha vane tyaktastavaiva putro bhadrāyunāmāsti iti tasya vṛtte kathite sati vajrabāhornijakarmaṇaḥ sasutapatnītyāgarūpasya lajjayā garhaṇānantaraṃ pratāpaśālinijaputraprāptyā'tyantānandaprāptiḥ, atha citrāṅgadena bhūpena kṛtaṃ pūjāsa- tkāramādāyātmano'gramahiṣīṃ tāṃ bhadrāyormātaraṃ svasnuṣayā sametaṃ bhadrāyuṣaṃ svaputraṃ ca gṛhītvā vajrabāhornijaparivārajanaiḥ saha mahatā samārambheṇa sānandaṃ svapurīṃ pratyāgamanam, tato bhadrāyunā pūrvaṃ piturājñayā yauvarājyaṃ kṛtvā pituḥ svargā- rohaṇānantaraṃ sarvabhūmaṇḍalarājyakaraṇam, rājyādhirohaṇānantaraṃ bhadrāyunā pūrvaṃ nibaddhasya hemarathākhyamāgadhabhūpasya maitrīṃ saṃdhāya bandhanānmocanam, tato bhadrāyunā svapatnyā kīrtimālinyā saha sukhopabhogapūrvakarājyakaraṇam, itthaṃ pūrvajanma- kṛtaśivayogipūjāsatkāraprabhāvavarṇanam ..... ..... 198 1

13 अथ ततः कदाचित्स्वल्पीयसैव समयेन तस्य शिवभक्तिं प्रकुर्वतो भद्रायोः
पितुर्वज्रबाहुनामकस्य दशार्णदेशभूपालस्य शत्रुणा मगधराजेन महता सैन्येन सह युद्धायागमनम्, ततो मगधराजेन दशार्णदेशभूपेन सह युद्धं कृत्वा युद्धे तं निर्जित्य तस्य सर्वं सैन्यं निर्णाश्य दशार्णदेशराष्ट्रं स्वायत्तीकृत्य तं रथे बद्ध्वा स्वदेशं प्रति गमनम्, इत्थं वैश्यनगरे निवसता भद्रायुराजपुत्रेण जनमुखान्निज-
पितृराष्ट्रविप्लववार्तां श्रुत्वा पद्माकरवैश्यपुत्रेण सुनयेन सहायेन हयमधिरुह्य महता जवेन निजपितृपालितं दशार्णदेशं मगधेश्वराख्यशत्रुभूपसैनिकैर्विध्वस्तं निरीक्ष्य ततः क्रोधावेशेन तूर्णमेव शत्रुसेनां प्रविश्य शिवयोगिदत्तविजयशंखमाध्माय विजयखड्गं चोद्यम्य सर्वाञ्छत्रुगणान्मूर्च्छनया विमोह्य बहुशः शत्रून्हत्वा शत्रुभी रथे निबद्धस्यात्मनः पितुर्बन्धान्मोक्षयित्वा शत्रुवशगाः सर्वाः स्वपितृपत्नीः पुरवासिजनानां पत्नीश्च कन्याश्च गोधनादीनि च मोचयित्वा स्वपित्रादीन्सर्वानाश्वास्य स्वपुर्यां संप्रेषणम्, ततोऽरिसैन्ये प्रवेशं कृत्वा तेषां स्त्रीगजाश्वरथदासदास्यादिसर्वसंपत्तिं हृत्वा मगधेशं पराजित्य समन्त्र्यादिपरिजनं तं निर्बध्य च स्वपुरीं प्रत्यागमनम्, अथ तेन भद्रायुना सुव्यक्तस्वनामाद्यकथयित्वैव
सामान्यतः क्षत्रियपुत्रत्वकथनपूर्वकं स्वपितुः पादाभिवन्दनकरणम्, अथ पितुर्नमनानंतरं तेन सुनयाख्येन वैश्यपुत्रेण सह भद्रायुणा वैश्यपुरं प्रत्यागत्य निजमात्रे तस्मै पद्माकराख्याय वैश्यवर्याय च सर्वयुद्धादिवृत्तान्तनिवेदनम्, अथ द्वितीयेऽह्नि चन्द्रांगदापरपर्यायं चित्राङ्गदं नृपं प्रति तस्य पूर्वोक्तस्यर्ष- भाख्यशिवयोगिन आगमनं चित्रांगदं प्रति भद्रायुषे राजपुत्राय कन्याप्रदा- नार्थमुपदेशपूर्वकमाज्ञाकरणं च, तत ऋषभयोगिवचनाच्चित्राङ्गदेन भूपेन भद्रा- युषमाहूय तस्मै कीर्तिमालिन्याख्यां निजकन्यां प्रदाय वैवाहिकविधिकरणाय समारम्भकरणम्, अथ तत्पितुर्वज्रबाहोः समीपे दूतं प्रेषयित्वा पुत्रस्योद्वाहार्थं सत्कारपूर्वकं निमन्त्रणम्, वज्रबाहोः सपरिवारस्य तत्र निषधेशराजधान्यामाग- मनम्, तस्यागतस्य पितुर्वज्रवाहोर्भद्रायुना पुत्रेणाभिवादनम्, तथाप्यविज्ञाततत्कु- लनाम्ना वज्रबाहुना तस्य भद्रायोर्जिज्ञासया प्रश्ने कृते सति निषधेश्वरेण वज्रबाहुं प्रति ऽअयं त्वया मात्रा सह वने त्यक्तस्तवैव पुत्रो भद्रायुनामास्ति इति तस्य वृत्ते कथिते सति वज्रबाहोर्निजकर्मणः ससुतपत्नीत्यागरूपस्य लज्जया गर्हणानन्तरं प्रतापशालिनिजपुत्रप्राप्त्याऽत्यन्तानन्दप्राप्तिः, अथ चित्राङ्गदेन भूपेन कृतं पूजास- त्कारमादायात्मनोऽग्रमहिषीं तां भद्रायोर्मातरं स्वस्नुषया समेतं भद्रायुषं स्वपुत्रं च गृहीत्वा वज्रबाहोर्निजपरिवारजनैः सह महता समारम्भेण सानन्दं स्वपुरीं प्रत्यागमनम्, ततो भद्रायुना पूर्वं पितुराज्ञया यौवराज्यं कृत्वा पितुः स्वर्गा- रोहणानन्तरं सर्वभूमण्डलराज्यकरणम्, राज्याधिरोहणानन्तरं भद्रायुना पूर्वं निबद्धस्य हेमरथाख्यमागधभूपस्य मैत्रीं संधाय बन्धनान्मोचनम्, ततो भद्रायुना स्वपत्न्या कीर्तिमालिन्या सह सुखोपभोगपूर्वकराज्यकरणम्, इत्थं पूर्वजन्म- कृतशिवयोगिपूजासत्कारप्रभाववर्णनम् ..... ..... 198 1
3.3.m: 13. Then, sometime after that, while that Bhadrāyus was practicing devotion to Śiva in a very short time, the king of Magadha, an enemy of his father named Vajrabāhu, the ruler of the Daśārṇa country, arrived for battle accompanied by a mighty army; then, the king of Magadha fought with the king of the Daśārṇa country, defeated him in battle, destroyed his entire army, brought the realm of the Daśārṇa country under his own control, bound him to a chariot, and departed toward his own country; thus, prince Bhadrāyus, residing in the merchants' city, heard from people's mouths the report of the devastation of his father's realm, mounted a horse with his companion Sunaya, the son of the merchant Padmākara, and with great speed saw the Daśārṇa country formerly protected by his father devastated by the soldiers of the enemy king, the lord of Magadha; then, overcome by anger, he immediately entered the enemy army, blew the conch of victory given by the Śiva yogin, raised the sword of victory, bewildered all the enemy hosts with a swoon, slew many enemies, freed his father who had been bound to a chariot by the enemies from his bonds, liberated all his father's wives who had fallen under enemy control, the wives and daughters of the townsfolk, and the cattle-wealth and so forth, consoled his father and all the others, and sent them to his own city; then, entering the enemy army, he seized all their wealth consisting of women, elephants, horses, chariots, male and female slaves, and so on, vanquished the lord of Magadha, bound him along with his ministers and retinue, and returned to his own city; then, without openly stating his own name and so forth, merely declaring himself to be the son of a kṣatriya, that Bhadrāyus offered salutations at his father's feet; then, after bowing to his father, Bhadrāyus returned to the merchants' city together with that merchant's son named Sunaya and reported the entire account of the battle and everything else to his mother and to that excellent merchant named Padmākara; then, on the second day, the previously mentioned Śiva yogin named Ṛṣabha approached King Citrāṅgada, otherwise called Candrāṅgada, and gave instruction and an order to Citrāṅgada to give his daughter in marriage to Prince Bhadrāyus; thereupon, upon the word of the yogin Ṛṣabha, King Citrāṅgada summoned Bhadrāyus, gave him his own daughter named Kīrtimālinī, and undertook the preparations to perform the marriage rites; then, he dispatched a messenger to the presence of his father Vajrabāhu and respectfully invited him to his son's wedding; Vajrabāhu arrived with his retinue there at the capital of the lord of Niṣadha; Bhadrāyus greeted his arrived father Vajrabāhu; nonetheless, as Vajrabāhu did not know his lineage and name, when he asked out of curiosity about Bhadrāyus, the lord of Niṣadha recounted his story to Vajrabāhu: 'This one, who was abandoned along with his mother in the forest by you, is your own son named Bhadrāyus'; upon that narration, Vajrabāhu, after reproaching himself with shame for his deed in abandoning his wife along with his son, experienced extreme joy at obtaining his own valiant son; then, accepting the honor and worship offered by King Citrāṅgada, taking his chief queen, who was Bhadrāyus's mother, and his son Bhadrāyus along with his daughter-in-law, Vajrabāhu returned to his own city with great celebration and joy together with his retinue; then, Bhadrāyus, having previously held the position of crown prince by his father's command, ruled over the entire circle of the earth after his father ascended to heaven; after ascending the throne, Bhadrāyus made an alliance of friendship and released from captivity the Magadhan king named Hemaratha, whom he had formerly imprisoned; then, Bhadrāyus ruled the kingdom enjoying pleasures together with his wife Kīrtimālinī; thus is the description of the efficacy of the worship and honor paid to the Śiva yogin in a past life. ..... ..... 198 1

3.3.s: 14 atha prāptarājyasiṃhāsanasya bhadrāyoḥ kadācinnijabhāryayā saha vanaṃ gatvā svacchanda- vihārakaraṇam, tasminneva samaye tasminvane kayościddvijadampatyormadhye vyāghre- ṇānugatyopadrave kriyamāṇe tābhyāṃ nijarakṣaṇārthamuccaiḥ śabdena rājñaḥ prārthanākaraṇam, tadaiva vyāghreṇāgatya dvijapatnyā grahaṇam, tasyopari bhadrāyuṇā vṛte'pi śastraprahāre sarvaśastrāṇāṃ vyarthībhāvaḥ, vyāghreṇa ca dvijapatnyāṃ hṛtāyāṃ dvijena śokapūrvakaṃ rājño dhikkārakaraṇam atha rājñā bhadrāyuṇā vyāghranāśitapatnīkasya tasya dvijasya sāntvanāya vahuvidhaprārthanākaraṇam, tato dvijena rājānaṃ prati nijakāmopabho- gaśāntyarthaṃ rājapatnīṃ prati yācanākaraṇam, tato bhadrāyuṇā tasmai brāhmaṇāya nijapatnīṃ dattvāgniṃ prajvālya śivaṃ dhyātvā'gnau patanāyodyamanam, tasminnevāvasare tadbhaktiparīkṣārthaṃ dvijarūpadhāriṇā tenaiva śrīśaṃkareṇa svasvarūpeṇa prādurbhavanam tasya śrīśaṃkarasya bhadrāyuṇā stutikaraṇam, tatstutiprasannena bhagavatā śrīśaṃkareṇa sapa- tnīkāya bhadrāyuṣe varapradānam, bhadrāyuṣaḥ śivaprasādādrājyasukhopabhogaprāptivarṇa- nam, ante ca putreṣu rājyaṃ vinyasya bhadrāyuṣaḥ śivasāyujyaprāptiḥ, bhadrāyuśvaśu- rasya citrāṅgadasya nijapatnyā sīmantinyā saha śāmbhavapadāvāptivarṇanam, itthaṃ śivabhaktimāhātmyavarṇanam... ....... ..... 200 1
3.3.d: 14 अथ प्राप्तराज्यसिंहासनस्य भद्रायोः कदाचिन्निजभार्यया सह वनं गत्वा स्वच्छन्द- विहारकरणम्, तस्मिन्नेव समये तस्मिन्वने कयोश्चिद्द्विजदम्पत्योर्मध्ये व्याघ्रे- णानुगत्योपद्रवे क्रियमाणे ताभ्यां निजरक्षणार्थमुच्चैः शब्देन राज्ञः प्रार्थनाकरणम्, तदैव व्याघ्रेणागत्य द्विजपत्न्या ग्रहणम्, तस्योपरि भद्रायुणा वृतेऽपि शस्त्रप्रहारे सर्वशस्त्राणां व्यर्थीभावः, व्याघ्रेण च द्विजपत्न्यां हृतायां द्विजेन शोकपूर्वकं राज्ञो धिक्कारकरणम् अथ राज्ञा भद्रायुणा व्याघ्रनाशितपत्नीकस्य तस्य द्विजस्य सान्त्वनाय वहुविधप्रार्थनाकरणम्, ततो द्विजेन राजानं प्रति निजकामोपभो- गशान्त्यर्थं राजपत्नीं प्रति याचनाकरणम्, ततो भद्रायुणा तस्मै ब्राह्मणाय निजपत्नीं दत्त्वाग्निं प्रज्वाल्य शिवं ध्यात्वाऽग्नौ पतनायोद्यमनम्, तस्मिन्नेवावसरे तद्भक्तिपरीक्षार्थं द्विजरूपधारिणा तेनैव श्रीशंकरेण स्वस्वरूपेण प्रादुर्भवनम् तस्य श्रीशंकरस्य भद्रायुणा स्तुतिकरणम्, तत्स्तुतिप्रसन्नेन भगवता श्रीशंकरेण सप- त्नीकाय भद्रायुषे वरप्रदानम्, भद्रायुषः शिवप्रसादाद्राज्यसुखोपभोगप्राप्तिवर्ण- नम्, अन्ते च पुत्रेषु राज्यं विन्यस्य भद्रायुषः शिवसायुज्यप्राप्तिः, भद्रायुश्वशु- रस्य चित्राङ्गदस्य निजपत्न्या सीमन्तिन्या सह शाम्भवपदावाप्तिवर्णनम्, इत्थं शिवभक्तिमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्... ....... ..... 200 1
3.3.m: 14. Then, Bhadrāyus, who had attained the royal throne, once went to the forest with his wife and roamed about at will; at that very time in that forest, when a tiger pursued and harassed a certain brahmin couple, they cried out loudly in supplication to the king for their own protection; right then the tiger came and seized the brahmin's wife; though blows with weapons were struck against it by Bhadrāyus, all the weapons became useless; and when the brahmin's wife was carried off by the tiger, the brahmin, filled with grief, reviled the king; then King Bhadrāyus made manifold appeals to console that brahmin whose wife had been destroyed by the tiger; then the brahmin begged the king for the queen in order to appease the longing of his own desire; then Bhadrāyus, giving his own wife to that brahmin, kindled a fire, meditated on Śiva, and prepared to throw himself into the fire; at that very moment, that very Lord Śaṃkara, who had assumed the form of the brahmin in order to test his devotion, manifested in his own true form; Bhadrāyus uttered a praise to Lord Śaṃkara; pleased by that praise, the blessed Lord Śaṃkara granted a boon to Bhadrāyus along with his wife; description of Bhadrāyus's attainment of the enjoyment of royal pleasures through Śiva's grace; and in the end, having entrusted the kingdom to his sons, Bhadrāyus's attainment of union with Śiva; description of the attainment of the state of Śambhu by Bhadrāyus's father-in-law Citrāṅgada along with his wife Sīmantinī; thus is the description of the greatness of devotion to Śiva. ... ....... ..... 200 1

15 atha bhasmamāhātmyavarṇanam tatprasaṅgena vāmadevākhyaśivayogino vṛttāntavarṇanam, tatraikadā krauñcāraṇye vicaraṃtaṃ taṃ vāmadevaśivayoginaṃ prati bhakṣituṃ samāgacchatā brahmarākṣasena nijadorbhyāṃ dṛḍhanipīḍane kṛte tadaṃgasparśamātrādeva tasya sadyo vidhva- stakalmaṣatāprāptiḥ, tato nijapūrvaduṣkarmasmaraṇena nirviṇṇamānasena tena brahmarākṣa- sena vāmadevaśivayoginaṃ prati nijapūrvapañcaviṃśatitamajanmācaritaduṣkarmatatpari- pākayāmyayātanābrahmarākṣasatvaprāptyādivarṇanam, tataśca vāmadevaṃ prati 'tvaddeha- sparśamātreṇa me pūrvasahasrajanmasmṛtijātāsti, mama cittaṃ ca suprasannaṃ vartate'ta etādṛśaḥ prabhāvastvayā kathaṃ labdhaḥ' iti praśne kṛte vāmadevaśivayoginā nijadeha- liptasya bhasmano'yaṃ prabhāva iti kathayitvā bhasmasāmarthyavarṇanam, tatprasaṃgena ca draviḍadeśasthadurācāravartibrāhmaṇasya pretopari bhasmaliptapādasya śunoṃ'ghrilagnabhasma- sparśanamātreṇa tasya brāhmaṇasya śivalokāvāptivṛttāntavarṇanam, itthaṃ vāmadevoktaṃ

3.3.m: 15. Now begins the description of the greatness of holy ash, and in that connection, the story of the Śiva-yogin named Vāmadeva. There, when that Śiva-yogin Vāmadeva was once roaming in the Krauñca forest, a brahmarākṣasa who came to devour him gripped him firmly with both arms; by the mere touch of his body, the [demon's] sins were instantly destroyed. Then, his mind filled with despondency at the memory of his past misdeeds, the brahmarākṣasa related to the Śiva-yogin Vāmadeva his evil deeds committed in his twenty-fifth past life, their fruition in the tortures of Yama, his attainment of the state of a brahmarākṣasa, and so forth. And then he asked Vāmadeva: 'By the mere touch of your body, memory of my past thousand births has arisen, and my mind has become exceedingly serene; so how did you attain such power?' Being thus questioned, the Śiva-yogin Vāmadeva stated, 'This is the power of the holy ash smeared on my body,' and described the efficacy of holy ash; and in that connection he related the story of how an ill-behaved brahmin residing in the Draviḍa country attained the world of Śiva by the mere touch of holy ash adhering to the foot of a dog whose paws were smeared with holy ash upon his corpse. Having thus heard the greatness of holy ash spoken by Vāmadeva, the brahmarākṣasa questioned Vāmadeva again in order to hear the greatness of holy ash in detail. [201.2]

3.3.m: 16. Now, as Vāmadeva began to describe the greatness of holy ash in detail, the arrival of all the gods, headed by Śakra, before the venerable Maheśa on Mandara, king of mountains, is described. In that great festival, all the gods worshipped and praised the blessed Maheśvara, who was seated upon a jewelled throne. And then, the great seer Sanatkumāra, in the course of inquiring about dharma set forth in the Vedas and Śāstras, questioned the exceedingly gracious blessed lord Rudra out of a desire to know the rule for wearing the tripuṇḍra. Hearing that question posed by him, the blessed lord Rudra described in detail the greatness of wearing the tripuṇḍra of holy ash. [203.1]

3.3.m: 17. Now, in connection with recounting the greatness of holy ash, the story of the Śabara is described: there, as Siṃhaketu, a prince of the Pāñcāla country, was once wandering in the forest for hunting, a Śabara, his follower who had gone along to assist him, saw a Śivaliṅga with a broken pedestal upon a sacrificial altar in the forest; taking it and approaching the prince, he asked him out of a desire to know the rite of worshipping the Śivaliṅga. Then, as a joke, the prince instructed him in the method of Śiva-worship with daily offerings of cremation ash and the like. That Śabara, having taken the liṅga to his house, devoutly brought cremation ash every day and worshipped the venerable Śaṃkara with the proper offerings according to the method spoken by the prince. Now once, being distressed because he could not obtain cremation ash for the Śiva-worship, his Śabarī wife consoled her husband, ignited their house with fire, and entered into it, burning her own body. Then, near his burnt house, with the cremation ash produced from the burning of his wife's body, the Śabara performed the complete worship of the venerable Śaṃkara; and at the conclusion of the worship, when he called out as usual to his Śabarī wife to receive the prasāda of the venerable Śiva, at that very moment she stood behind him as before, having returned as on every day; and his house too stood as before. Then, as he conversed with his wife in astonishment, a divine aerial chariot arrived; mounting that aerial chariot, the Śabara couple went to the world of Śiva and attained liberation through similarity of form with Śiva. Thus is described the greatness of steadfast faith. [204.2]

3.3.m: 18. Now begins the description of the greatness of the Umāmaheśvara observance, which grants the attainment of all ends; and in that connection, the story of Śāradā, the daughter of a brahmin named Vedaratha living in the Ānarta country, is described. There, when her husband, the brahmin Padmanābha, died of a snakebite, Śāradā, having attained widowhood, resided in her father's house. Once, having approached the great seer named Naidhruva who had arrived at her father's house, when Śāradā bowed to that aged, blind sage Naidhruva, the sage gave her the auspicious blessing: 'May you be fortunate with your husband and possessed of sons!' Then, having learned the fact of her widowhood, the sage Naidhruva instructed that Śāradā in detail regarding the performance of the Umāmaheśvara observance for the sake of obtaining good fortune. Then that Śāradā undertook the Umāmaheśvara observance taught by the sage. Then her parents and relatives requested the great seer Naidhruva to stay until the proper completion of her observance, so as to destroy the sorrow of Śāradā's widowhood; and at their request, the great seer Naidhruva stayed right there in the hermitage until the proper completion of the observance performed by Śāradā. [206.1]

strījanaiśca śāradāyāḥ sakāśādekānte saharṣaṃ satyavṛttāntaṃ vijñāya tasyāḥ praśaṃsāṃ kṛtvā svasvagṛhaṃ prati gamanam, atha śāradāyāḥ putrasantānotpattiḥ, tasya śārade- yākhyatya śāradāputrasya guruṇopanayane kṛte satyupanayanādanantaraṃ caturbhireva varṣai- ścaturvedādisāṅgopāṅgasamagravidyāpāraṃgatāvarṇanam ,atha kadācidgokarṇeśvaramahādevakṣetraṃ prati kasmiṃścicchivamahāparvaṇi 19 अथ शारदया तस्य स्वगुरोर्नैध्रुवमहर्षेः संनिधौ स्थित्वैकवर्षपर्यन्तं यथावि-
ध्युमामहेश्वरव्रताचरणम्, ततः संवत्सरांते तस्य व्रतस्योद्यापनकरणम्, उद्याप-
नदिनस्य रात्रौ तेन नैध्रुवमहर्षिणा तया शारदया सह जपध्यानतपोभिः श्रीजगदम्बायाः संतोषकरणम्, तस्मिन्नवसरे तयोर्भक्तिप्रभावाच्छ्रीजगदम्बायाः प्रादु-
भावः, तदानीमेव श्रीजगदम्बाप्रसादात्तस्यान्धस्य नैध्रुवमहर्षेश्चक्षुर्द्वयप्राप्तिः, ततो
नैध्रुवमहर्षिणा तया शारदया सह जगदम्बायाः स्तुतौ कृतायां सुप्रसन्नया जगदम्बया नैध्रुवमहर्षिप्रार्थनया शारदायाः पूर्वजन्मकर्मवर्णनपूर्वकम् ऽएतस्याः स्वप्ने स्वपतिना सह रतिसुखप्राप्तिर्भविष्यति' इति वरं प्रदाय शारदायै ऽनिजगर्भजातपुत्र स्वप्ने कृतभोगस्य पुरुषस्य यदा प्रत्यक्षं दर्शनं करिष्यसि तदा तस्मै देहि' इत्याज्ञां कृत्वान्तर्धानकरणम्, ततः सुप्रसन्नया तया शारदया बालया स्वगुरोनैध्रुवमुनेः पूजासत्कारकरणम्, ततो नैध्रुवमुनेः शारदापित्रो रहसि जगदम्बावर- प्रदानादिवृत्तं संश्राव्य सर्वानामन्त्र्य स्वेच्छया देशान्तरं प्रति गमनम् ,अथ शारदायाः श्रीजगदम्बायाः प्रसादेन स्वप्ने स्वभर्त्रा सह रतिसंभोगकरणाद्गर्भधारणम्,. ततो विधवां तां शारदां गर्भिणीं श्रुत्वा सर्वजनैर्धिक्कारकरणपूर्वकं तस्याः स्वग्रामाद्बहि- र्निर्वासनाय सर्वैः सहैकत्र मिलित्वा मन्त्रकरणम्, एवं तैर्जनैर्दुर्विचारे क्रियमाणे सत्याकाशवाण्या तस्याः शारदाया निर्दोषत्वकथनम्, तच्छुत्वा सुप्रसन्नैस्तैः सर्वजनैः स्त्रीजनैश्च शारदायाः सकाशादेकान्ते सहर्षं सत्यवृत्तान्तं विज्ञाय तस्याः प्रशंसां कृत्वा स्वस्वगृहं प्रति गमनम्, अथ शारदायाः पुत्रसन्तानोत्पत्तिः, तस्य शारदे- याख्यत्य शारदापुत्रस्य गुरुणोपनयने कृते सत्युपनयनादनन्तरं चतुर्भिरेव वर्षै- श्चतुर्वेदादिसाङ्गोपाङ्गसमग्रविद्यापारंगतावर्णनम् ,अथ कदाचिद्गोकर्णेश्वरमहादेवक्षेत्रं प्रति कस्मिंश्चिच्छिवमहापर्वणि तद्ग्रामस्थितानां यात्रार्थं प्रयाणे सति तैः सर्वस्व- ग्रामनिवासिभिर्जनैः सह तस्याः शारदाया अपि तेन स्वपुत्रेण सह गमनम् , तत्र तया शारदया नित्यं प्रति स्वप्ने रतिदायिनः पूर्वजन्मीयस्य विप्रस्य स्वभर्तु- दर्शनम्, तेनापि पुरुषेण प्रतिदिनं स्वप्ने रतिदायिन्यास्तस्याः शारदायाः स्वप्ने दृष्टस्य स्वस्मादुत्पन्नस्य तस्य पुत्रस्य च प्रत्यक्षदर्शनम्, ततस्तेन विप्रेण विस्मया- विष्टचित्ततया तत्समीपमागत्य शारदां प्रति तस्या वृत्तान्तजिज्ञासया प्रश्नक- रणम्, ततः शारदया तस्मै सर्वस्ववृत्तान्तनिवेदनम, ततस्तेन विप्रेण तद्दत्तं कुमारं तां शारदां च तस्याः पित्रोरनुज्ञया गृहीत्वा स्वगृहं प्रति गमनम्, ततः कालान्तरे तस्य विप्रस्य मरणोत्तरं चिताग्नौ शारदायास्तेन स्वभर्त्रा सहानुग- मनम, ततस्तयोर्दंपत्योः शिवलोकं प्रति गमनम. इत्थमुमामहेश्वरव्रतप्रभाववर्णनम्. ... ... ... 207 2
3.3.m: 19. Now begins the account of Śāradā staying in the presence of her guru, the great seer Naidhruva, and observing the vow of Umā-Maheśvara according to rule for one year; then, at the end of the year, performing the concluding rite of that vow; on the night of the day of the concluding rite, that great seer Naidhruva, together with Śāradā, pleasing the Mother of the Universe by recitation, meditation, and austerities; on that occasion, through the power of their devotion, the manifestation of the Mother of the Universe; at that very moment, by the grace of the Mother of the Universe, the blind great seer Naidhruva obtaining two eyes; then, when praise of the Mother of the Universe was offered by the great seer Naidhruva together with Śāradā, the Mother of the Universe, being well pleased, at the request of the great seer Naidhruva, having described Śāradā's deeds in her previous life, granted the boon: 'She shall obtain the pleasure of sexual union with her husband in a dream'; and having commanded Śāradā: 'Give the son born of your own womb to the man who enjoyed pleasure [with you] in the dream whenever you see him in person,' she vanished; then that young girl Śāradā, being well pleased, worshipped and honoured her guru, the sage Naidhruva; then the sage Naidhruva, having secretly related the account of the Mother of the Universe granting the boon and other events to Śāradā's parents, took leave of all and departed for another country according to his wish; now Śāradā, by the grace of the Mother of the Universe, conceiving a child from having sexual intercourse with her husband in a dream; then, hearing that the widow Śāradā was pregnant, all the people censured her and assembled together to deliberate upon exiling her from her own village; while such wicked thoughts were being entertained by those people, a voice from the sky declared the faultlessness of that Śāradā; having heard that, all those men and women, being well pleased, joyfully learned the true account from Śāradā in private, praised her, and went to their respective homes; now the birth of a male child to Śāradā; after the initiation of that son of Śāradā named Śāradeya was performed by the guru, the description of his attaining mastery within merely four years after initiation over the four Vedas and the entire body of learning along with their auxiliary and secondary branches; now, on a certain great festival of Śiva, when the residents of that village set out on a pilgrimage to the sacred field of the great god Gokarṇeśvara, that Śāradā also went along with her son together with all those residents of her village; there Śāradā saw her husband, the brahmin of her previous birth who daily granted sexual pleasure in dreams; that man too saw in person that Śāradā who daily gave sexual pleasure in dreams, and that son born of himself whom he had seen in the dream; then that brahmin, with his mind overwhelmed by wonder, approached her and questioned Śāradā out of a desire to know her story; then Śāradā reported her entire story to him; then that brahmin, having taken the boy given by her and that Śāradā with the permission of her parents, went to his own home; then, after a lapse of time, following the death of that brahmin, Śāradā's following her husband onto the funeral pyre; then the departure of the married couple to the world of Śiva. Thus ends the description of the power of the Umā-Maheśvara vow. ... ... ... 207 2

3.3.d: 20 अथ रुद्राक्षमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, तत्र रुद्राक्षधारणपुण्यवर्णनप्रसंगेन काश्मीरदेशनृपति- भद्रसेनसुतस्य सुधर्माख्यस्य राजामात्यसुतस्य तारकाख्यस्य चेत्युभयो राजपुत्रामात्यपुत्रयोर्बाल्यत आरभ्य परममैत्रीभावेन वर्तनम्, उभयोरपि सदैव हेमरत्न- मयालङ्कारपरित्यागपूर्वकं रुद्राक्षधारणेऽत्यन्तप्रेमाणं दृष्ट्वाऽतिविस्मयाविष्टेन राज्ञा भद्रसेनेनेकदा स्वगृहं प्रत्यागतं पराशरमुनिं प्रति पूजाविधिना सत्कृत्य तयोर्बाल- कयो रुद्राक्षधारणाभिरुचिकारणजिज्ञासया प्रश्नकरणम्, ततस्तेन पराशरमह- र्षिणा तयो राजपुत्रामात्यपुत्रयोः पूर्वजन्मवृत्तान्तवर्णनम्, तत्र पूर्वं नन्दिग्राम- निवासिन्या महावैभवशालिन्याः सदा सदाशिवपूजानिरताया महानन्दानाम्न्याः कस्याश्चिद्वेश्यायाः सद्मनि निवसतोः कुक्कुटमर्कटयो रुद्राक्षकृतकर्ण-बाहु-चूडा- भरणयोर्वेश्यया प्रतिदिनं कृतायां नृत्यशिक्षायां प्रावीण्यं प्राप्तयोः प्रतिदिनं तस्या वेश्यायाः शिवाग्रतो नृत्यसमये नृत्यम्, अथ कदाचित्तस्या भवनं कस्य- चिच्छिवव्रतधारिणः शिवयोगिनो वैश्यस्यागमनम्, तत्करे दिव्यरत्नकंकणं दृष्ट्वा तल्लिप्सया तया वेश्यया तस्मै वैश्याय स्वस्या वारांगनात्वे सत्यपि ऽत्रिदिन- पर्यन्तं ' तव पत्नीत्वं स्वीकृत्य सहधर्मचारिणीधर्मेणाऽहं त्वां सेविष्ये' इति प्रतिज्ञाकरणम्, ततश्च तेन शिवव्रतपरायणेन वैश्येन तस्या वचनमाकर्ण्य बाढमित्युक्त्वा तस्या हस्ते निजनित्यपूजनीयरत्नमयशिवलिङ्गं दत्त्वैतस्य रत्नमयशिवलिङ्गस्य नाशे मम प्राणनाशः स्यादिति कथयित्वा तस्य लिङ्गस्यातिप्रयत्नेन संरक्षणायाज्ञाकरणम्, तया महानन्दावेश्यया तस्य वैश्यस्याज्ञां संमान्य तद्दत्तं लिङ्गमादाय नाट्यमण्डपिकास्तम्भोपरि तल्लिंगं निधाय स्वगृहं प्रविश्य रात्रौ तेन वैश्येन पर्यंके सुखेन संगतया निद्राकरणम्, ततो निशीथसमयेऽकस्मादुत्थितेन वह्निना तस्या वेश्यायाः सर्वनाट्यमण्डपस्य दहनम् ,तस्मिन्नवसरे सद्यः प्रबुद्धया तया वेश्यया तत्र सत्वरमेत्य रज्ज्वा शृंखलया च निबद्धयोः तयोः कुक्कुटमर्कटयोः सत्वरं बन्धनतो मोचनम्, मोचितयोस्तयोः कुक्कुटमर्कटयोस्तस्मान्मण्डपस्थलाद्वह्निभीत्या दूरे पलायनम्, सर्वमण्डपदाहे सति मण्डपस्थस्तम्भस्य तदुपरि निहितस्य वैश्यदत्तरत्नमयलिङ्गस्य च दहनेन शकलीभवनम्, तल्लिङ्गनाशं दृष्ट्वा तेन वैश्येन मरणाय निश्चयं कृत्वा चिता- निर्माणाय तां महानन्दावेश्यां प्रत्याज्ञाकरणम्, ततस्तस्य वैश्यस्य दृढनिर्बन्धं दृष्ट्वा तया वेश्यया ग्रामाद्बहिः काष्ठैश्चिताया निर्माणम्, ततः प्रज्वालितायां तस्यां चितायां तेन शिवभक्तेन वैश्येन प्रवेशकरणम्, तं वैश्यं चितां प्रविष्टं दृष्ट्वाऽतिखिन्नया तया महानन्दया वेश्यया तेन त्रिरात्रं पत्नीत्वप्रतिज्ञाना- त्सहधर्मचारिणीधर्मं पुरस्कृत्य शिवभक्तेभ्यः स्वकीयं सर्वस्वं प्रदाय तमग्निं त्रिः परिक्रम्य शिवं स्मृत्वा तस्मिन्नग्नौ पत्यनुगमनाय प्रवेशकरणायोद्यमनम्, तदानीं साक्षाद्भगवता शंकरेण तत्र प्रादुर्भूय तस्या निवारणं कृत्वा स्वस्यैव भक्तिपरीक्षणाय वैश्यरूपेणागमनादि कथयित्वा सर्वपरिवारजनैः सह तस्या महानन्दाया वेश्यायाः शिवलोकं प्रति नयनम्, तत्परिवारजनेष्ववशिष्टयोर्गृह- दहनसमये बन्धनाद्विमुच्य दूरं पलायितयोस्तयोः कुक्कुटमर्कटयोः स्वस्वकालेन मरणे सति मर्कटस्य राजपुत्रत्वं कुक्कुटस्य चामात्यपुत्रत्वं संप्रति संप्राप्तमिति पराशरेण राजपुत्रामात्यपुत्रयोः पूर्वजन्मवृत्तान्तकथनम्... ...... 210
3.3.m: 20. Now begins the description of the māhātmya of rudrākṣa beads. In that context, on the occasion of describing the spiritual merit of wearing rudrākṣa beads, [there is an account of] the prince named Sudharman, son of King Bhadrasena of the country of Kāśmīra, and the minister's son named Tāraka, both of whom, from their childhood onward, lived in consummate friendship. Having witnessed in both of them an extraordinary love for wearing rudrākṣa beads to the constant exclusion of ornaments made of gold and gems, King Bhadrasena, filled with great wonder, once honored Sage Parāśara who had arrived at his palace according to the prescribed rites of worship, and inquired out of a desire to know the cause of those two boys' fond attachment to wearing rudrākṣa beads. Thereupon the great sage Parāśara described the account of the previous lives of the prince and the minister's son. In former times, in the house of a courtesan named Mahānandā—who dwelt in Nandigrāma, possessed immense opulence, and was constantly devoted to the worship of Sadāśiva—there lived a rooster and a monkey adorned with ear, arm, and crest ornaments made of rudrākṣa beads, who had attained mastery in the training in dance given daily by the courtesan and who used to dance daily in front of Śiva at the time of that courtesan's dance. Then, once, a certain vaiśya who observed the vow of Śiva and was a Śaiva ascetic arrived at her house. Seeing a celestial jewel-bracelet on his hand and desiring to obtain it, that courtesan, even though she was a professional courtesan, made a vow to that vaiśya: 'Having accepted the role of your wife for three days, I shall serve you in accordance with the duty of a lawful wife.' Hearing her words, that vaiśya, who was intent upon the vows of Śiva, said 'So be it,' placed in her hands a jeweled Śivaliṅga that was his object of daily worship, and commanded her to protect that liṅga with the utmost care, saying, 'If this jeweled Śivaliṅga is destroyed, it will be the end of my life.' Respecting that vaiśya's command, the courtesan Mahānandā took the liṅga given by him, set that liṅga atop a pillar of the dance pavilion, entered her house, and slept at night happily joined with that vaiśya upon the couch. Then at midnight, due to a fire that suddenly broke out, the entire dance pavilion of that courtesan burned down. At that moment, that courtesan, awakened immediately, went there swiftly and promptly freed from bondage that rooster and monkey who had been tied with a rope and a chain. Those two, the rooster and the monkey, having been freed, fled far away from that pavilion out of fear of the fire. When the whole pavilion burned, the pillar standing in the pavilion and the jeweled liṅga placed upon it, given by the vaiśya, broke into fragments from the burning. Seeing the destruction of that liṅga, that vaiśya resolved to die and commanded the courtesan Mahānandā to prepare a funeral pyre. Then, seeing that vaiśya's firm insistence, that courtesan constructed a pyre outside the village with pieces of wood. Then, when that pyre was ignited, that vaiśya, a devotee of Śiva, entered it. Seeing that vaiśya had entered the pyre, that courtesan Mahānandā, deeply grieving, in view of her vow of wifeliness for three nights, placed foremost the duty of a faithful wife, bestowed all her possessions upon the devotees of Śiva, circumambulated that fire three times, remembered Śiva, and prepared to enter that fire in order to follow her husband in death. At that moment, the Blessed Lord Śaṃkara manifested there in visible form, restrained her, declared that he had come in the form of a vaiśya to test her devotion, and led that courtesan Mahānandā, along with all the members of her household, to the world of Śiva. Of those remaining among the members of her household, that rooster and monkey who had been released from bondage at the time of the burning of the house and had fled far away, died in due course of time, and the monkey has now attained the state of the prince, while the rooster has attained the state of the minister's son—thus Parāśara related the account of the previous lives of the prince and the minister's son. ... 210

3.3.s:
21 atha rājñā bhadrasenena tasya rājakumārasya bhaviṣyadbhāgyaviṣaye parāśaramuniṃ prati pṛcchāyāṃ kṛtāyāṃ parāśaramuninā tasya sudharmākhyasya rājaputrasyādyadinātsaptame'hni mṛtyurbhaviṣyatīti bhaviṣyatkathanam, tacchutvā'tiduḥkhitaṃ bhadrasenabhūpaṃ prati bodha- vacanaiḥ samāśvāsya tasya sudharmākhyarājaputrasya mṛtyunivāraṇāya rudrādhyāyajapā- nuṣṭhānakathanam, atha rājñaḥ prārthanayā rudrādhyāyapāṭhapūrvakaṃ tena parāśaramuninā vratatapaḥsadācārasaṃpannairbrāhmaṇaiḥ saha tasya rājakumārasya pratidinamabhiṣeke kriya- māṇe saptame'hnyakasmātkṣaṇamātraṃ mūrchanā prāpya punaḥ sadya eva prabodhanam, tadānīṃ tena kumāreṇa mūrchanāvasthāyāṃ mṛtyoḥ śivadūtasya cāgamanapūrvakaṃ śivadūtakṛta- mṛtyuparābhavakathanam, tataḥ parāśarādibhiḥ sarvairṛṣibhistasya rājakumārasyāśīrvacanaṃ pradāya tatpitre rājñe'bhayaśaṃsanam, tato rājñā sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ vipulaambāyāḥ bhojanapradānādinā satkārakaraṇam, tataḥ svaputreṇa parāśaraguruprabhṛtimaharṣibhiśca
saha siṃhāsana upaviṣṭasya suprasannasya tasya bhadrasenanṛpasya sramīpe mahāyoginaḥ
śrīnāradamaharṣerāgamanam, tato bhadrasenena rājñā kṛtapūjāsatkriyeṇa nāradena rājānaṃ prati 'tava putraṃ netuṃ yamasyātrāgamane sati śaṃkareṇa preṣitena vīrabhadreṇa yamasya śāsanaṃ kṛtam iti varṇanaṃ yamena vīrabhadrasya praṇāmapūrvakaṃ stutikaraṇānaṃtaraṃ vīrabha-
drādyamamocanādivṛttāntavarṇanaṃ ca, 'rudrādhyāyapaṭhanapūrvakābhiṣecanaprabhāvāttava putrasya
mṛtyubhītinivāraṇaṃ jātamasyāyutavarṣaparyaṃtamāyuḥ sakalasaukhyāvāptiśca bhaviṣyati'
ityāśīḥ pradāya nāradasya gamanam, parāśarādimaharṣīṇāṃ ca sahaputrāya rājña āśīḥ
pradāya svasvāśramagamanam, itthaṃ rudrādhyāyaprabhāvavarṇanam... ..... 211 2
3.3.d:
21 अथ राज्ञा भद्रसेनेन तस्य राजकुमारस्य भविष्यद्भाग्यविषये पराशरमुनिं प्रति पृच्छायां कृतायां पराशरमुनिना तस्य सुधर्माख्यस्य राजपुत्रस्याद्यदिनात्सप्तमेऽह्नि मृत्युर्भविष्यतीति भविष्यत्कथनम्, तच्छुत्वाऽतिदुःखितं भद्रसेनभूपं प्रति बोध- वचनैः समाश्वास्य तस्य सुधर्माख्यराजपुत्रस्य मृत्युनिवारणाय रुद्राध्यायजपा- नुष्ठानकथनम्, अथ राज्ञः प्रार्थनया रुद्राध्यायपाठपूर्वकं तेन पराशरमुनिना व्रततपःसदाचारसंपन्नैर्ब्राह्मणैः सह तस्य राजकुमारस्य प्रतिदिनमभिषेके क्रिय- माणे सप्तमेऽह्न्यकस्मात्क्षणमात्रं मूर्छना प्राप्य पुनः सद्य एव प्रबोधनम्, तदानीं तेन कुमारेण मूर्छनावस्थायां मृत्योः शिवदूतस्य चागमनपूर्वकं शिवदूतकृत- मृत्युपराभवकथनम्, ततः पराशरादिभिः सर्वैरृषिभिस्तस्य राजकुमारस्याशीर्वचनं प्रदाय तत्पित्रे राज्ञेऽभयशंसनम्, ततो राज्ञा सर्वेषां ब्राह्मणानां विपुलअम्बायाः भोजनप्रदानादिना सत्कारकरणम्, ततः स्वपुत्रेण पराशरगुरुप्रभृतिमहर्षिभिश्च
सह सिंहासन उपविष्टस्य सुप्रसन्नस्य तस्य भद्रसेननृपस्य स्रमीपे महायोगिनः
श्रीनारदमहर्षेरागमनम्, ततो भद्रसेनेन राज्ञा कृतपूजासत्क्रियेण नारदेन राजानं प्रति ऽतव पुत्रं नेतुं यमस्यात्रागमने सति शंकरेण प्रेषितेन वीरभद्रेण यमस्य शासनं कृतम् इति वर्णनं यमेन वीरभद्रस्य प्रणामपूर्वकं स्तुतिकरणानंतरं वीरभ-
द्राद्यममोचनादिवृत्तान्तवर्णनं च, ऽरुद्राध्यायपठनपूर्वकाभिषेचनप्रभावात्तव पुत्रस्य
मृत्युभीतिनिवारणं जातमस्यायुतवर्षपर्यंतमायुः सकलसौख्यावाप्तिश्च भविष्यति'
इत्याशीः प्रदाय नारदस्य गमनम्, पराशरादिमहर्षीणां च सहपुत्राय राज्ञ आशीः
प्रदाय स्वस्वाश्रमगमनम्, इत्थं रुद्राध्यायप्रभाववर्णनम्... ..... 211 2
3.3.m: 21. Now, when King Bhadrasena questioned the sage Parāśara regarding the future destiny of the prince, the sage Parāśara foretold the future, stating that on the seventh day from today, death would befall the prince named Sudharma; hearing this, [Parāśara] consoled the deeply grieved King Bhadrasena with words of wisdom and prescribed the performance of the recitation of the Rudrādhyāya to avert the death of that prince named Sudharma; then, at the king's request, as daily ceremonial baths were performed for the prince by that sage Parāśara together with brahmins endowed with vows, austerities, and virtuous conduct, accompanied by the recitation of the Rudrādhyāya, on the seventh day he suddenly fell into a swoon for a mere moment and then immediately regained consciousness; then that prince narrated the arrival of Death and of a messenger of Śiva during his state of swoon, and the defeat of Death wrought by Śiva's messenger; then Parāśara and all the other seers, bestowing blessings upon the prince, gave assurance of safety to his father, the king; then the king honoured all the brahmins by providing abundant food and other offerings; then, while King Bhadrasena was seated delightfully upon his throne together with his son and the great seers headed by the teacher Parāśara, the great yogin, the revered sage Nārada, arrived in his presence; then Nārada, having been honoured and worshipped by King Bhadrasena, described to the king: 'When Yama came here to take your son, Yama was chastised by Vīrabhadra, who was sent by Śaṃkara', along with the account of Yama's bowing, praising, and subsequent release by Vīrabhadra; and giving the blessing, 'By the power of the ceremonial bath accompanied by the recitation of the Rudrādhyāya, your son's fear of death has been dispelled; he will attain a lifespan of ten thousand years and all happiness,' Nārada departed; and the great seers headed by Parāśara, bestowing blessings upon the king and his son, departed to their respective hermitages; thus is described the efficacy of the Rudrādhyāya. ... 21

3.3.s:
22 atha śibabhaktimāhātmyapratipādaka puṇyamayapurāṇakathāpaṭhanaśravaṇavidhipūrvaka phalavarṇanam, purāṇaśravaṇamāhātmyavarṇanaprasaṃgena jārakarmapravṛttayorvidurākhya brāhmaṇādhamabindulākhyatatpatnyorvṛttāntavarṇanam, tatra jārakarmaṇā veśyāsaktena vidurākhyabrāhmaṇādhamena nityaṃ jāreṇa saha saṃgatāmapi kasmiṃścidekasmindine jāreṇa saha ratāsaktāṃ jāriṇīṃ svabhāryāṃ dṛṣṭvā tāṃ prati saṃtāḍya 'tvaṃ jārebhyo ratiṃ dattvā tebhyo dhanamādāya mahyaṃ veśyāyai dhanapradānāya dehi tenāhaṃ veśyāyāṃ ramiṣye tvaṃ jārai ramasva' ityuktyā pratidinamubhayorapyadhamayostayordurācāre pravṛttiḥ, itthaṃ kiyatā kālena tasya brāhmaṇādhamasya maraṇānaṃtaraṃ kiṃcidutkrāntayauvanāyāstasyā biṃdulākhyāyā jārotpannairnijaputraiḥ svakīyairbāṃdhavaiśca saha kadācitparvaviśeṣe gokarṇakṣetraṃ prati yātrārthaṃ gamanam, tatra gatvā kasmiściddevālaye paurāṇikena purāṇe vācyamāne tayā biṃdulayā
tasya paurāṇikasya mukhātpurāṇaśravaṇasamaye jārasaktānāṃ nārīṇāṃ smaramandire yamakiṅkarāḥ saṃtaptalohaparighaṃ kṣipanti ' iti yamayātanāvṛttāṃtaṃ śrutvā satatakṛta-
svakīyajāraduṣkarmasmaraṇasaṃtaptahṛdayayā tayā biṃdulayā rahasi taṃ paurāṇikaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ prati gatvā nijaduṣkarmapariśāntaya upāyajijñāsayā praśnakaraṇam, tatastena paurāṇikena tasyāḥ purāṇaśravaṇamātreṇa nijaghoravyabhicārapāpasmaraṇenātyugrayamayātanābhītāyā biṃdulākhyāyāḥ sāṃtvanapūrvakaṃ śivabhaktipuraḥsaraśivanāmamantroccāraṇapūrvaka śivabhaktipratipādaka purāṇakathāśravaṇopadeśakaraṇam, tatastayā bindulayā tasmādeva paurāṇikātsadguroḥ sakāśācchivabhaktivarddhakapurāṇakathāśravaṇam, purāṇaśravaṇaprabhāvāttasyā vindulāyāḥ śanaiḥśanai rajastamomaladhvaṃse jāte sati hṛdaye
śrīśaṅkarasya praveśaḥ, tataḥ pratidinaṃ tayā gurūpadiṣṭamārgeṇa śrīśaṅkarasya bhaktika-
raṇam, śrīśivabhaktiprabhāvāttayā nikhilakarmabaṃdhaṃ samācchidyānte śivalokaṃ prati
gamanam, tatra śivaloke śrīpārvatījagadambāyāḥ samīpe gatāyāstasyāḥ pārvatyā
saṃmānakaraṇam, tataḥ pārvatyāḥ sakāśānnijabhartuḥ piśācatvaprāptiṃ śrutvā tasya nijabhartuḥ piśācayonermokṣāya tayā tuṃbaruṃnāma gandharvaṃ prati viṃdhyaśaile sthitāya nijabhartre purāṇaśrāvaṇārthaṃ prārthanākaraṇam, tayā prārthitena tuṃbaruṇā viṃdhyaśailaṃ gatvā
taṃ piśācaṃ prati śrīgaurīpatikathāyāḥ śrāvaṇe kṛte tasya piśācatvaṃ prāptasya biṃdulā-
pateḥ piśācayonito muktipūrvakaṃ vimānamāruhya śivalokaṃ prati gamanavarṇanam ,
tatastayordaṃpatyoḥ śrīmaheśvarasadguṇagāyanena kaivalyamuktiprāptivarṇanam, śrīśivabha-
ktipratipādakabrāhmottarakhaṇḍapuṇyākhyānavaibhavavarṇanapūrvakaṃ brāhmottarakhaṇḍasamāptiva-
rṇanam. - .. - ... 213 2
3.3.d:

3.3.m: 22. Now, the description of the rules and fruits of reciting and hearing the meritorious Purāṇic tales that establish the greatness of devotion to Śiva; in connection with describing the greatness of hearing the Purāṇa, the account of the vile brahmin named Vidura and his wife named Bindulā, who were engaged in adultery, is related: there, that vile brahmin named Vidura, addicted to a prostitute through adulterous deeds, one day saw his adulterous wife passionately engaged in lovemaking with a paramour—though she consorted daily with paramours—and struck her, saying, 'Give pleasure to lovers, take money from them, and give it to me to provide money for the courtesan; through that, I shall enjoy the courtesan, and you may enjoy lovers'; by this agreement, both vile persons engaged in misconduct daily; thus, after some time, upon the death of that vile brahmin, that woman named Bindulā, whose youth was somewhat past, went on a certain auspicious festive occasion with her sons born of paramours and her relatives on a pilgrimage to the sacred field of Gokarṇa; having gone there, while the Purāṇa was being recited by a Purāṇa reciter in a temple, Bindulā heard from the mouth of that Purāṇa reciter the account of the tortures of Yama: 'The servants of Yama thrust red-hot iron bars into the private parts of women addicted to lovers'; her heart burning with constant recollection of her own adulterous misdeeds, Bindulā approached that brahmin reciter of the Purāṇa in secret and inquired about the means to expiate her evil deeds; then that reciter of the Purāṇa, having consoled Bindulā—who was terrified of the fierce tortures of Yama merely by hearing the Purāṇa and remembering her grave sin of adultery—instructed her to hear the Purāṇic narratives establishing devotion to Śiva, accompanied by devotion to Śiva and the chanting of the name and mantras of Śiva; then Bindulā listened from that very Purāṇa reciter, her true guru, to the Purāṇic tales that increase devotion to Śiva; through the power of hearing the Purāṇa, when the impurities of rajas and tamas were gradually destroyed in Bindulā, the revered Śaṃkara entered her heart; then, following the path instructed by her guru, she practiced devotion to the revered Śaṃkara daily; through the power of devotion to the revered Śiva, having severed all bondage of karma, she went at the end of her life to the realm of Śiva; there in the realm of Śiva, when she approached the revered Pārvatī, Mother of the Universe, she was honoured by Pārvatī; then, having heard from Pārvatī of her husband's attainment of the state of a piśāca, she made a supplication to the gandharva named Tumburu to recite the Purāṇa to her husband who dwelt on the Vindhya mountain, for the sake of his liberation from the womb of a piśāca; Tumburu, besought by her, went to the Vindhya mountain and recited the story of the Lord of Gaurī to that piśāca, whereupon the description is given of how Bindulā's husband, who had become a piśāca, attained liberation from the state of a piśāca and, mounting an aerial chariot, went to the realm of Śiva; then is described how the couple attained absolute liberation through singing the auspicious virtues of the revered Maheśvara; and the conclusion of the Brāhmottarakhaṇḍa is narrated, accompanied by the description of the majesty of the holy legend of the Brāhmottarakhaṇḍa that establishes devotion to the revered Śiva. ... 22
Thus ends the third section, the Brāhmottarakhaṇḍa, in the Brāhmakhaṇḍa. (3-3)
Thus ends the third section, the Brāhmakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa. 3
